Rejoni closed a $25 million financing in June 2026 with ClavystBio, Amed Ventures, Ascension Ventures, Catalyst Health Ventures, Delos Capital, FemHealth Ventures, Iyengar Capital and Sparta Group, and appointed women's health MedTech leader John Nealon as chief executive officer in May 2026. Rejoni runs no developer program and publishes no public API: its entire web presence is a small Webflow marketing site, and probes for OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL, MCP, llms.txt and every /.well-known/ discovery path returned HTTP 404 against a verified real-404 origin, while api./developer./docs./app./portal.rejoni.com resolve only to a wildcard A record with no listener answering on either port 80 or 443.

providers.name: Revolution Medicines
providers.description: Revolution Medicines is a clinical-stage precision oncology company headquartered in Redwood City, California, developing targeted therapies for RAS-addicted cancers. Its pipeline centers on RAS(ON) inhibitors — including daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), zoldonrasib (RMC-9805), and elironrasib (RMC-6291) — designed to directly target the active, GTP-bound (ON) state of oncogenic RAS proteins across mutations such as KRAS G12X. The company pairs structure-based drug discovery with clinical development to pursue treatments for pancreatic, lung, colorectal, and other RAS-driven tumors. Revolution Medicines is a publicly traded corporate entity (Nasdaq: RVMD) and does not currently expose a public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Topos Bio
providers.description: Topos Bio is an AI-native drug discovery company building all-atom foundation models for intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) — dynamic, flexible proteins implicated in diseases such as Alzheimer's and prostate cancer. Its Topos-1 foundation model generates physically realistic conformational ensembles for flexible proteins, aiming to make previously undruggable targets therapeutically viable. The company is backed by Threshold Ventures. No public API or developer platform is currently published.

providers.name: Vial
providers.description: Vial is a next-generation biotech company advancing first and best-in-class biologics to treat unmet need in Immunology and Inflammation. The company pairs AI-driven drug discovery with automated, technology-enabled clinical trials, working across target discovery (identifying high-value therapeutic targets), molecule design (generating and optimizing molecular candidates), and experimental validation (high-throughput approaches to accelerate development). Its lead pipeline program is an IL-13 x TSLP bi-specific antibody in Phase 1. Vial was originally built as a tech-enabled contract research organization (CRO) focused on reimagining clinical trials, and was backed by General Catalyst. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Vial publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Clinflash
providers.description: Clinflash (易迪希医药科技 / Clinflash Healthcare Technology) is a Chinese clinical-research technology company founded in 2014 that provides a cloud-based clinical trial information platform for pharmaceutical sponsors, CROs, and research sites. Its self-developed suite spans more than ten systems, including Clinflash EDC (electronic data capture), IRT/IWRS (randomization and trial supply management), eCOA/ePRO (electronic clinical outcome and patient-reported outcomes), Safety/PV (pharmacovigilance and drug-safety alerting), CTMS (clinical trial management), eTMF (electronic trial master file), eCTD, eConsent, eSign, Coder (medical coding), and ePAY (subject payment). Clinflash has supported thousands of clinical trial projects for over a thousand pharmaceutical, generic, medical-device, and IVD organizations, including pivotal Phase III and international multi-center studies. The platform is delivered as a login-gated SaaS at cloud.clinflash.com and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer/API program, OpenAPI, SDKs, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: Orchestra Bio
providers.description: Orchestra (orchestra.bio) is an agentic operations platform for drug development and life sciences R&D organizations, helping teams unify planning across leadership, programs, and scientific groups, automate R&D workflows, and reduce the operational risks that derail breakthrough science. The San Francisco company pairs unified program roadmaps with intelligent operations and decision support, and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), 8VC, Haystack, and other investors. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Orchestra publishes a product marketing site, a company blog, and a hosted web application, but no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Tierra Biosciences
providers.description: Tierra Biosciences is a San Leandro, California synthetic biology company using AI-guided, cell-free protein production to synthesize custom proteins on demand for pharmaceutical, industrial, and agricultural research. Its customer-facing Tierra Protein Platform is a web-based eCommerce ordering portal where researchers enter protein sequences and get custom proteins synthesized, validated, and shipped. The company (rebranding toward Revr Bio) is backed by prosus-ventures and Material Impact. No public developer API, SDK, or programmatic-access surface is currently published; this profile was enriched and confirmed as a web-platform-only provider.

providers.name: 10x Science
providers.description: 10x Science is an AI-native software company building the first AI-native protein characterization platform for the life sciences, starting with drug development. A Y Combinator W26 company founded out of Nobel laureate Carolyn Bertozzi's laboratory at Stanford University, it automates peptide mapping for protein therapeutics, delivering explainable molecular insights in minutes where legacy tools and manual workflows take months. The company raised a $4.8M seed round led by Initialized Capital and is headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company; it does not yet publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Abogen
providers.description: Abogen Biosciences (Suzhou Abogen Biosciences Co., Ltd. / 苏州艾博生物科技有限公司) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in January 2019 and headquartered in Suzhou, China, dedicated to developing transformative medicines through messenger RNA (mRNA) innovation. The company has built full-scale in-house capabilities spanning the entire mRNA drug development cycle - protein engineering, mRNA sequence design and synthesis, proprietary lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery, formulation, and commercial-scale manufacturing. Its product pipeline covers infectious disease prevention and cancer immunotherapy, and it has advanced an EUA mRNA product along with additional clinical-stage candidates. Abogen is a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund. Abogen is a pharmaceutical / biotechnology company and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this profile captures its corporate identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: CAMP4 Therapeutics
providers.description: CAMP4 Therapeutics is a clinical-stage RNA-medicines biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, pioneering a new class of antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapeutics designed to increase targeted gene expression. Built on the company's RAP Platform (Regulatory RNA Activating Platform), which combines epigenomics, computational biology, and machine learning to map the regulatory RNA and signaling circuits controlling gene expression, CAMP4 develops first-in-class medicines for diseases caused by insufficient protein expression, with an initial focus on central nervous system and metabolic disorders such as urea cycle disorders and SYNGAP1. Founded by CEO Josh Mandel-Brehm with scientific co-founders Rick Young (Whitehead Institute/MIT) and Len Zon (Boston Children's Hospital/Harvard), CAMP4 is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). This is a corporate/therapeutics company profile in the API Evangelist network; CAMP4 publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal, so no API artifacts apply.

providers.name: Gilgamesh Pharma
providers.description: Gilgamesh Pharma (Gilgamesh Pharmaceuticals, Inc.) is a New York based clinical-stage neuroscience company founded in 2019 that develops rapid-acting, next-generation therapeutics for psychiatric and substance use disorders. Its discovery and translational platform combines medicinal chemistry, neurocircuitry science, electrophysiology and machine learning to identify new chemical entities, and its pipeline spans short-acting 5-HT2A receptor agonists, NMDA receptor antagonists, non-hallucinogenic neuroplastogens, cardiac-safe ibogaine analogs and M1/M4 muscarinic programs. Lead assets include bretisilocin (GM-2505), acquired by AbbVie in August 2025, and blixeprodil (GM-1020), an orally bioavailable NMDAR antagonist in Phase 2 for major depressive disorder. Gilgamesh is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Kytopen
providers.description: Kytopen Corp. is a Cambridge, Massachusetts life-sciences instrument company, spun out of MIT, that builds non-viral, continuous-flow cellular engineering hardware for cell and gene therapy discovery and manufacturing. Its Flowfect technology combines continuous fluid flow with electric fields to deliver mRNA, DNA and CRISPR payloads into cells, and is sold as two benchtop platforms: Flowfect Discover, an automated small-volume system that runs up to 96 high-throughput transfections in about ten minutes, and Flowfect TX, a closed-system instrument that processes 10-50 million cells per mL at 25-50 mL per minute for GMP-scale manufacturing. The company sells laboratory instruments and consumables to biopharma and CDMO customers through a quote and technology-access motion; it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. Instrument data integration for Flowfect customers is delivered by a third party, Ganymede Bio, under its own platform and its own contract - that surface belongs to Ganymede, not to Kytopen.

providers.name: Medeor Therapeutics
providers.description: Medeor Therapeutics is a clinical-stage cellular immunotherapy company in San Mateo, California, developing MDR-101, a one-time cell therapy manufactured from a living kidney donor's blood that induces mixed chimerism so HLA-matched transplant recipients can withdraw from lifelong immunosuppression while preserving graft function. The platform originated in roughly two decades of research at Stanford University led by Dr. Samuel Strober. The company completed a Phase 3 registration trial that exceeded its target success rate, and has since suspended operations and is seeking an acquirer to complete the BLA filing. Medeor is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it publishes no developer portal, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Ratio Therapeutics
providers.description: Ratio Therapeutics Inc. is a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company headquartered at One Design Center Place in Boston, Massachusetts, developing next-generation precision radiopharmaceuticals for solid tumors. Founded in 2022 by Jack Hoppin, Ph.D. and John Babich, Ph.D., the company pairs two proprietary R&D platforms — Trillium, a tunable albumin-binding targeting scaffold that modulates pharmacokinetics, and Macropa, a bifunctional chelator built for the alpha emitter actinium-225 — to improve drug availability, tumor delivery and tumor loading. Its lead program, [Ac-225]RTX-2358, is a FAP-targeted radiotherapeutic in the ATLAS Phase 1/2 trial, alongside a next-generation GRPR program, mono- and bispecific radioligand therapies, and PET imaging assets. Ratio has licensing and collaboration agreements with Novartis, Merck, Bayer and Lantheus, isotope supply agreements with Nusano, TerraPower Isotopes and PanTera, and manufacturing partnerships with PharmaLogic and Eckert & Ziegler. It closed a $70 million Series C in July 2026, bringing total capital raised past $240 million. Ratio is a therapeutics developer rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Satellite Bio
providers.description: Satellite Bio is a biotechnology company developing off-the-shelf liver cell therapies to treat severe and life-threatening liver diseases. Its tissue therapeutics platform engineers functional hepatocytes designed to engraft and restore liver function, combining the biological power of liver cells with scalable manufacturing and distribution. The company is headquartered in Newton, Massachusetts and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Satellite Bio is a life-sciences company and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Viatris
providers.description: Viatris Inc. is a global healthcare company formed in November 2020 through the combination of Mylan and Pfizer's Upjohn division. Viatris is one of the world's largest producers of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and generic medicines, serving patients in more than 165 countries. The company has undergone significant strategic restructuring, divesting its India API business and women's healthcare business. Viatris focuses on branded generics, complex generics, biosimilars, and branded specialty medicines. No public developer API program or developer portal has been identified; the company operates in B2B pharmaceutical supply chain contexts without a public technology integration API offering.

providers.name: Bio-Rad Laboratories
providers.description: Bio-Rad Laboratories is a global leader in developing and manufacturing a wide range of products for the life science research and clinical diagnostic markets, including instruments, reagents, consumables, software, and services. Founded in 1952, Bio-Rad serves scientists in genomics, proteomics, cell biology, quality control, and clinical diagnostics with products like real-time PCR systems, western blotting instruments, flow cytometers, and digital PCR.

providers.name: Healthpeak Properties
providers.description: Healthpeak Properties (NYSE: DOC) is an S&P 500 healthcare real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns, operates, and develops real estate for healthcare discovery and outpatient care — concentrated in lab/life-sciences, outpatient medical, and continuing care retirement community (CCRC) senior housing segments. The company tagline is "Where Discovery and Outpatient Care Thrive." Originally founded as HCP Inc. in 1985, the company rebranded to Healthpeak Properties in 2019. On March 1, 2024, Healthpeak completed an all-stock merger of equals with Physicians Realty Trust, combining two of the largest outpatient medical real estate platforms in the United States and adopting the new NYSE ticker DOC (previously PEAK). Healthpeak's portfolio spans roughly 700 properties nationwide, with lab concentrations in the South San Francisco, Boston, and San Diego clusters (including Torrey Pines Science Park and The Cove at Oyster Point) and outpatient medical assets clustered on or near top-ranked hospital campuses such as Medical City Dallas. The company reports that approximately 150,000 scientists, researchers, physicians, and healthcare professionals work in its buildings. As a healthcare REIT, Healthpeak does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or technical integration surface. Its public digital footprint is limited to corporate marketing, an investor relations site, SEC filings, ESG/sustainability reporting, and a press room. Tenant-facing operational systems (work orders, building access, energy reporting) are not exposed externally.

providers.name: firsthand
providers.description: firsthand is a healthcare company delivering peer-based support to individuals living with serious mental illness and substance use disorders, helping them access care, benefits, and community resources. Its guides and specialists have lived experience of mental illness, and its HITRUST r2-certified helpinghand platform coordinates care across states including Florida, Ohio, Michigan, Virginia, and Washington. firsthand is a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; firsthand publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Revagenix
providers.description: Revagenix, Inc. is a private clinical-stage precision-therapeutics company headquartered in San Francisco, California, founded in 2019 by antibacterial-discovery veterans from Achaogen. The company takes a first-principles approach to drug design for serious chronic disease, engineering each candidate around target biology, route of delivery and tolerability. Its lead program, Rev-56, is a first-in-class inhaled precision therapy with a novel mechanism of action targeting chronic Pseudomonas infection in non-cystic-fibrosis bronchiectasis (NCFB), a progressive respiratory disease affecting an estimated 350,000 to 500,000 adults in the United States; Rev-56 is entering Phase 1 clinical development in 2026, with a dry-powder formulation approaching candidate selection. Revagenix is backed by Novo Holdings, Tenmile, the REPAIR Impact Fund and the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID contract 75N93022C00061). Revagenix is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Reven Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Reven Pharmaceuticals is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 1999 and headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado. Reven develops medicines from its proprietary RJX Technology platform - a patented, first-in-class intravenous composition of anti-oxidant and anti-inflammatory ingredients - and is advancing candidates for sepsis, multi-system inflammation, cytokine release syndrome, ARDS and vascular, oncology, CNS and ocular indications. Its lead candidate, Rejuveinix (RJX), completed a double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 dose-escalation study in healthy volunteers and received FDA clearance of an Investigational New Drug application for the treatment of COVID-19. Reven publishes a corporate and investor website at reven.com covering its pipeline, modalities, clinical trials, expanded-access program and news, but operates no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable interface of any kind.

providers.name: Ten63 Therapeutics
providers.description: Ten63 Therapeutics is an AI-driven drug-discovery company spun out of Duke University in 2019 and operating from San Francisco, Durham and Boston. It builds BEYOND, which the company describes as the world's first Large Quantum Chemistry Model — pairing generative chemistry at scale (Move37) with a quantum-accurate forcefield and molecular-dynamics engine (Astrolabe) in an approach it calls Superlearning. BEYOND is used to design therapeutics for previously undruggable and under-drugged targets, with an internal pipeline focused on oncology and platform partnerships such as the multi-target collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim. Ten63 is a therapeutics company, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract. It does publish an llms.txt describing the company and platform for AI agents.

providers.name: Transition Bio
providers.description: Transition Bio is a preclinical drug discovery company built on biomolecular condensate science, operating as a joint spin-out of the University of Cambridge and Harvard University with sites in Cambridge, Massachusetts and Cambridge, United Kingdom. The company combines droplet-microfluidics high-throughput molecular screening with a machine learning engine to identify and optimize small molecules that modulate intrinsically disordered proteins and the condensates they form, an approach the company has described as its Condensomics platform. It was seeded in November 2020 and closed a $50 million Series A in June 2022 led by Northpond Ventures with Taiho Ventures, Bristol Myers Squibb and Magnetic Ventures participating, and in November 2025 announced a collaboration with Voyager Therapeutics on small molecules targeting TDP-43 in ALS and frontotemporal dementia. Transition Bio is a therapeutics developer rather than a software or data vendor: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Astraea
providers.description: Astraea is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) clinical trial automation platform that gives pharmaceutical sponsors, biotechs, and CROs an AI operating system for clinical development. Founded by Joshua Wang and Sanmay Sarada, the platform orchestrates specialized AI agents across the full biometrics lifecycle - standards mapping, data normalization, CDISC mapping, SDTM and ADaM dataset generation, TFLs/TLFs, SAP, eCRFs, Define-XML, QC, and submission documents - turning a protocol and raw study data into FDA-submission-ready output. Astraea is positioned as sponsor-run software rather than a CRO: it runs inside the customer's own secure environment so clinical data never reaches Astraea's servers, with 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and audit-ready, standards-native traceability. The company reports serving 10+ global pharma and biotech sponsors with 30-50% faster reporting cycles.

providers.name: Chroma Medicine
providers.description: Chroma Medicine was a Boston-based, clinical-stage biotechnology company developing epigenetic editors — CRISPR-derived medicines that silence or activate genes by writing epigenetic marks rather than cutting DNA — with CRMA-1001, a liver-targeted epigenetic editing therapy for chronic hepatitis B and hepatitis D, as its lead program. In December 2024 it merged with Nvelop Therapeutics, pairing Chroma's epigenetic editors with Nvelop's non-viral in vivo delivery vehicles, to form nChroma Bio with $75 million in new financing. chromamedicine.com now redirects to nchromabio.com. As a therapeutics developer it publishes no developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: DermBiont
providers.description: DermBiont, Inc. is a Boston, Massachusetts clinical-stage dermatology therapeutics company founded in 2017 that develops targeted topical treatments addressing the root cause of skin disease rather than its symptoms. Its lead program SM-030 is a first-in-class topical PKC-beta inhibitor in development for melasma and other hyperpigmentation disorders of the skin, targeting excess melanin production; earlier programs included SM-020 for seborrheic keratosis and the live-bacterial DBI-001 and DBI-002 candidates for atopic dermatitis, tinea pedis and onychomycosis. The company describes an in-house discovery platform for microbiome-based therapeutics built on terabytes of DNA sequencing data from human skin samples across healthy individuals and patients, paired with a proprietary computational biology platform that identifies functions gained and lost by the skin microbiome. That computational platform is internal research tooling, not a product: DermBiont sells drug candidates and partnering opportunities, publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind, and its website is a Squarespace-hosted corporate site.

providers.name: Mettler-Toledo International
providers.description: Mettler-Toledo is a global manufacturer of precision instruments and services for use in laboratories, manufacturing, and food retailing applications. This repository captures the APIs, developer tools, and machine-readable API artifacts for Mettler-Toledo International.

providers.name: Shennon Biotechnologies
providers.description: Shennon Biotechnologies is a San Francisco based biotechnology company accelerating drug development by screening millions of single cell-cell interactions to identify novel therapeutic agents for cancer and autoimmune disease. Its proprietary TCELERATOR platform combines ultrafast single cell-cell interaction mapping with proprietary AI models to discover new targets and develop more effective medicines. The company is backed by DCVC and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes a corporate marketing site but no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Retro Biosciences
providers.description: Retro Biosciences is a Redwood City, California longevity biotechnology company founded in 2021 whose stated mission is to add ten years to healthy human lifespan. Its published preclinical pipeline spans RTR242, a small-molecule autophagy-flux booster aimed at Alzheimer's disease; RTR888, iPSC-derived microglial progenitors for CNS conditions; RTR890, iPSC-derived hematopoietic stem cells for blood disorders; AAV-delivered in vivo tissue reprogramming for osteoarthritis and age-related hearing loss; and AI-designed protein therapeutics, the last built on a 2025 collaboration with OpenAI on a protein-engineering model for reprogramming factors. Retro was seeded with $180M from Sam Altman and reported a $1.8B valuation in 2026. It is a therapeutics company rather than a software company: it operates a public GitHub organization of internal lab-automation and bioinformatics tooling, but publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Arrakis
providers.description: Arrakis Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company pioneering RNA-targeted small molecules (rSMs) as a new class of genetic medicines. Its rSM platform enables orally available small molecules to bind RNA and modulate previously undruggable biological pathways, with an industrialized discovery toolkit spanning multiple modalities. The lead proprietary program targets Type 1 Myotonic Dystrophy (DM1) at the root cause of the disease, alongside a pipeline of proprietary and partnered programs. A GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company in the life-sciences sector, Arrakis was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it publishes a corporate and scientific website but no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Arrakis Therapeutics
providers.description: Arrakis Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company pioneering RNA-targeted small molecules (rSMs) — orally available small-molecule medicines designed to bind directly to RNA and reach targets long considered undruggable. Its rSM Platform and rSM Toolkit industrialize the discovery and development of these medicines across proprietary and partnered programs, with a lead candidate addressing the root cause of Type 1 Myotonic Dystrophy (DM1). Based in Waltham, Massachusetts, the company is backed by Canaan Partners. This profile is part of the API Evangelist network; Arrakis Therapeutics does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Aspen Neuroscience
providers.description: Aspen Neuroscience is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing personalized regenerative cell therapies for Parkinson's disease. Its lead candidate, ANPD001, is an autologous induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived neuron replacement therapy that uses a patient's own cells to restore dopamine function without requiring immunosuppression, with manufacturing designed for scalable, reproducible production. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network. It operates a corporate website only and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or specification surface at this time; artifact coverage here is limited to domain/identity signals.

providers.name: Athos Therapeutics
providers.description: Athos Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Torrance, California developing precision small-molecule therapeutics for autoimmune and chronic inflammatory diseases, led by co-founder and CEO Dr. Dimitrios Iliopoulos. Its AI/ML discovery platform integrates multi-omic patient data — genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, epigenomics, metabolomics and microbiomics — collected with global hospital systems to identify novel drug and gene targets, and produced ATH-063, an AI-generated G9A methyltransferase inhibitor advancing in inflammatory bowel disease. The computational side of the business is commercialized through Chiron AI Labs (formerly AthosOmics.AI), a deliberately no-code omics analysis SaaS suite (Athos-Multi, Athos-T, Athos-P, Athos-G, Athos-PM) that is pre-launch and gated behind a demo waitlist. Athos publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Bexorg
providers.description: Bexorg, Inc. is a New Haven, Connecticut and San Francisco based digital-biology company building AI-powered drug-discovery infrastructure for central nervous system (CNS) therapies. Its BrainEx platform restores and sustains whole donated human brains to test drug candidates directly in human tissue, generating clinically predictive data on blood-brain-barrier delivery, target engagement, and brain exposure across small molecules, biologics, viral vectors, and lipid nanoparticles before human trials. Backed by Amplify Partners, Bexorg aims to reduce the high failure rate of CNS clinical trials. The company markets a scientific platform and does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Biotree
providers.description: Biotree (Shanghai Biotree Biomedical Technology, 百趣生物) is a Shanghai-based life-sciences company founded in 2012 that provides mass-spectrometry-driven metabolomics, proteomics, transcriptomics, and multi-omics products and services. It operates non-targeted and high-throughput targeted metabolomics platforms, single-cell and spatial omics, pharmaceutical protein characterization, clinical diagnostic test kits, and CDMO services, backed by a proprietary compound spectral library of 20,000+ standards, automated sample-preparation systems (Starlid), a LIMS, and the MAPS cloud analysis portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API or specification is published at this time.

providers.name: Cure Genetics
providers.description: Cure Genetics (克睿基因) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in 2016 and based in Suzhou, Jiangsu, China, developing cell and gene therapies for solid tumors and genetic diseases. Its differentiated pipeline is built on two proprietary platforms: AIMS CAR-NKT, a cell-therapy approach engineered to improve solid-tumor infiltration and modulate the tumor microenvironment, and VELP, an AAV (adeno-associated viral) vector technology targeting the nervous system, heart, and kidneys. Lead programs include CGC729, an anti-CD70 CAR-NKT therapy in Phase I trials for renal cell carcinoma, and CGC-602, a PD-1-IL-2v bispecific molecule for cancer immunotherapy. The company is backed by Qiming Venture Partners, Advantech Capital, and Oriza Holdings. It publishes no public API, developer platform, or technical documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record surfaced from the Qiming portfolio.

providers.name: Inscinstech
providers.description: Inscinstech (Suzhou Inscinstech Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd.) is a Chinese life-sciences instrumentation manufacturer serving the biopharmaceutical industry. It designs and builds equipment for oligonucleotide and nucleic-acid synthesis, chromatography and protein purification, tangential-flow filtration, bioreactors and cell culture, nanomedicine (LNP) preparation, high-pressure preparative liquid chromatography, peptide synthesis, and analytical instruments (HPLC, capillary electrophoresis, pumps and valves), spanning laboratory, pilot, and production scale. It also delivers end-to-end process solutions for oligonucleotide drugs, mRNA, peptides, and recombinant proteins. The company is backed by Qiming Venture Partners. It is a hardware and instruments provider and publishes no public developer API surface at this time; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Moonwalk Biosciences
providers.description: Moonwalk Biosciences is a preclinical biotechnology company pioneering therapeutics in adipose biology driven by deep genetic and epigenetic insights. Co-founded by Feng Zhang, Alex Aravanis, Arash Jamshidi and Justin Valley, the company developed a multiplex epigenetic engineering platform and has publicly shifted its focus toward siRNA-based obesity and cardiometabolic therapies. It is a private, research-stage drug-discovery organization backed by GV; its public surface is a corporate/marketing website covering its science, pipeline, team, careers and news, with no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable discovery documents.

providers.name: Orca Bio
providers.description: Orca Bio is a late-stage biotechnology company, headquartered in Menlo Park, California with a cGMP manufacturing facility in Sacramento, developing high-precision allogeneic cell therapies for cancer and autoimmune diseases. Its single-cell sorting platform separates donor blood with high purity and speed to build proprietary, precisely-defined mixtures of immune and stem cells. Orca Bio's lead program TREGZI is a precision-engineered allogeneic T-cell immunotherapy for hematological malignancies, alongside investigational programs Orca-T and Orca-Q. As a clinical/therapeutics company it does not publish a public developer or API surface; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Felicis and enriched with verified company identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Orchestra
providers.description: Orchestra is an agentic operations platform for drug development and life sciences R&D organizations. The software helps biotech and pharmaceutical teams unify planning, automate operations, and reduce the risks that derail breakthrough science by creating centralized roadmaps across leadership, programs, and scientific groups, applying AI agents to operational automation, and delivering data-driven decision support across scenarios, planning, and CRO management. Orchestra is a portfolio company of 8vc and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a marketing and product site only and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Profusa
providers.description: Profusa, Inc. (Nasdaq: PFSA) is a South San Francisco digital-health and medical-device company that builds tissue-integrated biosensors — injectable, biologically compatible hydrogel microsensors smaller than a grain of rice — for continuous, real-time monitoring of body chemistry. Its Lumee Oxygen Platform reports tissue oxygen for peripheral artery disease, chronic wounds and reconstructive surgery, and a long-duration Lumee glucose sensor is in development. A companion Data Platform turns raw sensor readings into clinical intelligence for clinicians, with EMR integration described as planned rather than shipped. Profusa has received more than USD 23M in NIH and DARPA funding and became publicly traded in July 2025 through a business combination with NorthView Acquisition Corporation. As of this profiling pass the company publishes no developer program, no public API documentation and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: SonoThera
providers.description: SonoThera, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered at 201 Haskins Way in South San Francisco, California, founded in 2022 to make genetic medicine deliverable without a viral vector. Its RIPPLE platform pairs an intravenously administered lipid-and-microbubble formulation with an externally applied diagnostic ultrasound probe: the acoustic energy transiently permeabilizes cell membranes in the targeted organ so a nucleic-acid payload enters only where the probe is pointed, an approach built on the roughly 35 million ultrasound contrast-agent doses given safely each year in cardiac imaging. A companion payload engineering platform, PORE, carries DNA and RNA constructs, gene editing and gene silencing cargo of varied size and format. The company holds an exclusive license to GE HealthCare's Optison and Sonazoid microbubble products for use with the platform, and has raised approximately $186 million — a $60.75 million Series A and an oversubscribed $125 million Series B — from ARCH Venture Partners, Johnson & Johnson, Illumina Ventures and Eli Lilly, to push lead programs in Duchenne muscular dystrophy and autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease into the clinic, with preclinical work in Alport syndrome and hemophilia A. It was co-founded by Kenneth Greenberg (CEO), Steve Feinstein (Chief Scientific Officer) and Michael H. Davidson (Executive Chairman). SonoThera sells therapeutics, not software: it runs no developer program, publishes no API, SDK or machine-readable specification, and maintains no public source-code organization.

providers.name: Tessera Therapeutics
providers.description: Tessera Therapeutics is an early-stage life sciences company, founded and backed by Flagship Pioneering, pioneering Gene Writing — a new category of genetic medicine designed to write therapeutic messages into the genome to treat and potentially cure disease at its source. Its Gene Writing platform uses mobile genetic elements delivered via lipid nanoparticles to insert genes and exons, make small insertions and deletions, or change single or multiple DNA base pairs, with applications spanning sickle cell disease, in vivo CAR-T, HIV, and other monogenic, metabolic, autoimmune, and neurodegenerative diseases. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a health-tech portfolio lead; Tessera is a therapeutics developer and does not currently publish a public developer or API surface.

providers.name: 83 Sciences
providers.description: 83 Sciences is an AI-native materials-discovery company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) that helps research labs unlock value from unpublished and discarded experimental data. Roughly 90% of experimental data never reaches publication; 83 Sciences works on-site with researchers to capture and structure that hidden data into a queryable database, then applies AI-powered analysis and generative models to learn from a lab's full experimental history — including failed experiments — to surface novel materials, co-authored manuscripts, and patents. Founded by researchers from MIT, Stanford, Harvard, and Columbia and based in San Francisco. The company currently ships no public API or developer surface; this profile tracks its identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Alinea Health
providers.description: Alinea Health is an AI-powered clinical trial recruitment intelligence platform that analyzes global trial registry data (ClinicalTrials.gov, ISRCTN, EU CTR) alongside patient availability to detect enrollment risk before it causes delays and to match eligible patients to appropriate studies for sponsors, CROs, sites, and healthcare providers. The platform surfaces at-risk trials, benchmarks sites, and visualizes enrollment pipelines, positioning delay prevention as protecting $1.1M-$1.7M per month in trial spend. The company advertises enterprise-grade RESTful APIs and custom data pipelines with end-to-end encryption and SOC 2 compliance, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; access is gated behind a partner platform and an early-access program. Backed by General Catalyst, with offices in Toronto and Barcelona.

providers.name: Alpha Biopharma
providers.description: Alpha Biopharma is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Shanghai, China, with an additional office in Beijing. The company focuses on the clinical development and commercialization of global innovative drugs across oncology and immunotherapy, spanning medical affairs, clinical operations, regulatory affairs and commercialization. Its lead product is Zorifertinib (formerly AZD-3759, marketed as Zorifer), a next-generation EGFR TKI designed for EGFR mutation positive advanced NSCLC patients with central nervous system metastases, which received NMPA approval in November 2024 as the first EGFR-TKI indicated for lung cancer with brain metastases. Alpha Biopharma also partners with Wugen Inc. on universal off-the-shelf memory NK and CAR-T cell therapies. The company raised a Series A led by Qiming Venture Partners. Alpha Biopharma publishes a corporate marketing website only and operates no public API, developer portal, or software platform.

providers.name: Ankyra Therapeutics
providers.description: Ankyra Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing "anchored" immunotherapies for cancer and immune-mediated diseases. Its proprietary platform tethers immune-modulating drugs to aluminum hydroxide so that treatment concentrates locally at the disease site, broadening the therapeutic window while reducing systemic toxicity and dosing frequency. The lead candidate, ANK-101, is an anchored IL-12 therapy in clinical evaluation for patients with advanced solid tumors. Ankyra is backed by investors including Google Ventures (GV), Mithril, Polaris Partners, Sands Capital, and Fidelity. The company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical platform; this profile exists in the API Evangelist network for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Ansun Biopharma
providers.description: Ansun Biopharma is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in the Sorrento Valley district of San Diego, California, founded in 2003 by virologists and molecular biologists and led by CEO Dr. Nancy Chang. Rather than targeting viruses directly, Ansun develops host-directed immuno-biologic therapies built on a recombinant sialidase platform. Its lead candidate, DAS181 (Ansun-181), is a multi-function sialidase fusion protein that removes the sialic acid receptors respiratory viruses use to enter host cells, and has been studied in parainfluenza virus (PIV), severe influenza, human metapneumovirus and COVID-19 in immunocompromised and hospitalized patients. The company also advances earlier-stage programs in oncology and autoimmune disease from the same sialidase platform. Ansun is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes a corporate WordPress site covering its pipeline, research and technologies, publications, intellectual property, investors, news and careers, and exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Atropos Health
providers.description: Atropos Health is a Stanford-spinout, New York / Bay Area real-world evidence (RWE) company founded in 2020 by Nigam Shah, Brigham Hyde, and Saurabh Gombar to close the medical "evidence gap" by converting routine healthcare data into publication-grade observational studies in minutes instead of months. Its flagship platform GENEVA OS (Generative Evidence Acceleration Operating System) is a federated, cloud-agnostic operating system that installs behind the customer's firewall, ingests longitudinal patient records as in-memory patient-timeline objects, and exposes a Temporal Query Language (TQL) and Advanced Cohort Engine (ACE) for rapid observational analyses without moving PHI. On top of GENEVA OS, Atropos offers ChatRWD, a conversational chat-to-database application that generates full observational studies from natural-language clinical questions, the Atropos Evidence Agent (an agentic AI deployed at Stanford Health Care and developed in collaboration with Microsoft to surface RWE directly inside clinical workflows and notes), Green Button (the original on-demand consult-style evidence service that gave rise to the company), Forge (study automation), and Alexandria, marketed as the world's largest body of precision evidence-based findings with 33M+ entries used for clinical decision support and LLM training. The company sells into health systems (pharmacy, research informatics, value-based care, GME) and life sciences (brand planning, HEOR, medical affairs, R&D, commercial analytics, precision-medicine AI/ML), is backed by Valtruis, Emerson Collective, Breyer Capital, McKinsey Ventures, Cencora Ventures, Presidio Ventures, Merck Global Health Innovation, Samsung Next, and others, and partners with Stanford Health Care, Mayo Clinic Platform, and Microsoft. Atropos has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release; GENEVA OS, TQL, ACE, ChatRWD, and the Evidence Agent are proprietary enterprise software delivered under contract to health-system and life-sciences customers, and the company's public GitHub org contains only forks (FAISS, HELM, security-policy-templates, terraform-aws-github-runner) and a small number of internal research notebooks rather than any shippable client library.

providers.name: BioTheryX
providers.description: BioTheryX is a private, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, discovering and developing first-in-class targeted protein degraders — both bifunctional degraders and molecular glues — for cancer and inflammatory disease. Its proprietary PRODEGY platform is built on Cereblon-binding expertise carried over from founders who worked on FDA-approved Cereblon modulators. The lead program BTX-9341, a dual CDK4/CDK6 degrader, is in Phase 1 for HR+/HER2- breast cancer, alongside BTX-10908 targeting SOS1 for pan-KRAS mutant cancers and PDE4 degraders for inflammatory conditions; the company also partners with Incyte on molecular glue degrader discovery. BioTheryX is a therapeutics developer with no public developer program: probes on 2026-08-02 returned 404 for /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs, /llms.txt and every /.well-known/ discovery path on biotheryx.com, and there is no api./developer./docs./portal. subdomain, GitHub organization, or published SDK.

providers.name: CytomX Therapeutics
providers.description: CytomX Therapeutics is a clinical-stage, oncology-focused biopharmaceutical company based in South San Francisco, California, pioneering a novel class of masked, conditionally activated biologic therapeutics built on its proprietary Probody platform. The Probody technology is engineered to remain inactive in healthy tissue and to become selectively unmasked and activated within the tumor microenvironment, with the goal of producing more potent, less toxic cancer medicines. The company's pipeline spans antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), T-cell engaging bispecific antibodies, and immunotherapies, advanced both internally and through partnerships with major pharmaceutical companies. CytomX is a publicly traded company (Nasdaq CTMX). This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners; as a biopharmaceutical research organization CytomX does not publish a public developer API, so this profile carries company identity and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Duane Morris
providers.description: Duane Morris LLP is a Philadelphia-headquartered, full-service U.S. and international law firm founded in 1904 by Russell Duane, Steven Heckscher, and Roland S. Morris. Chaired by Matthew A. Taylor, the firm describes itself as "a law firm with more than 900 attorneys in offices across the United States and internationally" — with a U.S. footprint spanning the East Coast, Texas, the Mountain West, and California, plus international offices in London, Singapore, Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City), Shanghai, Myanmar, and joint ventures/alliances reaching Mexico and Latin America. An Am Law 100 firm since 2001, Duane Morris is known for depth in intellectual property (including patent prosecution and PTAB practice), trial and appellate litigation, real estate, corporate transactions, employment, healthcare, cannabis, and life sciences. The firm publishes an extensive LexBlog-powered thought-leadership network of more than 50 practice-area blogs, all of which expose RSS 2.0 feeds via the standard WordPress /feed/ convention. Duane Morris does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec, GraphQL endpoint, webhooks, status page, or developer portal; the GitHub organization github.com/duanemorris exists but has no public repositories. The firm's only machine-readable surfaces are the RSS feeds of its blog network.

providers.name: FindMeCure
providers.description: FindMeCure is a Sofia, Bulgaria healthtech company (founded 2015, backed by Techstars) that connects patients with clinical trials through a patient-facing search engine often described as "the Google of clinical trials," letting people search, find, and join a trial within a few clicks. Its sister B2B product, TrialHub, is a clinical-trial strategy, feasibility, and patient-recruitment intelligence platform covering 70 countries and serving pharmaceutical sponsors and CROs including Takeda, Novartis, and Syneos Health. No public developer API is currently documented; this profile captures the company's identity and probed domain security posture.

providers.name: Immune-Onc Therapeutics
providers.description: Immune-Onc Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Palo Alto, California, founded in 2016 by Charlene Liao and Guo Liang Yu. The company develops novel antibody therapeutics that target myeloid cell inhibitory receptors — with a current focus on the Leukocyte Immunoglobulin-Like Receptor subfamily B (LILRB) — to treat blood cancers, solid tumors, and autoimmune and inflammatory disease. Its clinical pipeline includes IO-108, a fully human IgG4 antagonist antibody targeting LILRB2 (ILT4) in Phase 1b/2 for solid tumors including hepatocellular carcinoma, and IO-202, a first-in-class IgG1 antibody targeting LILRB4 (ILT3) in Phase 1b for acute myeloid leukemia and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, which holds FDA Fast Track and Orphan Drug designations. Preclinical programs include IO-312, a LILRB4-directed bispecific antibody, and IO-106 targeting LAIR1. The company has clinical collaborations with BeiGene, Regeneron, and Roche, and has raised approximately $138 million across Series A and Series B financings from investors including Northern Light Venture Capital, Vivo Capital, CLI Ventures, and the Stanford-StartX Fund. Immune-Onc is a therapeutics developer, not a software or platform company: as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no SDKs, no public GitHub organization and no /.well-known/ discovery surface — its only machine-readable documents are two Squarespace RSS feeds for its news and press-release collections. This record therefore captures the company's verified public identity, its published web properties, its clinical-trial registry presence, and the probed security posture of its public web surface.

providers.name: Until Labs
providers.description: Until Labs (branded "until") is a San Francisco deep-tech biotechnology company developing reversible cryopreservation technology for human donor organs. Its mission is to build a "pause button for biology" by safely vitrifying organs at ultra-low temperatures without ice formation, then rewarming them for transplant — extending the viability window for donor organs and improving transplant outcomes. The company builds perfusion hardware, cryoprotective agents, cooling and rewarming infrastructure, and organ-health assessment methods, working toward whole-body medical hibernation. Co-founded by Laura Deming and Hunter Davis, Until has raised over $100M including a $58M Series A (September 2025) led by Founders Fund with Lux Capital participating. As a wet-lab hardware and life-sciences company, Until publishes no public developer API, SDK, or software platform. This profile was surfaced as a Lux Capital portfolio company and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: Valthos
providers.description: Valthos is a New York City-based biodefense company developing frontier AI systems that identify biological threats and design medical countermeasures in real time. The company emerged from stealth in October 2025 with $30 million in backing from the OpenAI Startup Fund, Lux Capital, and Founders Fund, with a founding team drawn from Palantir, DeepMind, the Broad Institute, and the Arc Institute. Valthos is building AI-powered biodefense infrastructure to rapidly analyze biological sequences and update medicines at scale for experts in government and the life sciences. The company does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or open-source surface.

providers.name: BociMed
providers.description: Shanghai BociMed Pharmaceutical Research Co., Ltd. (上海博志研新药物研究有限公司) is a Chinese pharmaceutical CRO/CDMO founded in 2012 in the Zhangjiang Pharmaceutical Valley, Shanghai, with an R&D headquarters in Zhangjiang, a production base in Lingang, and a clinical subsidiary in Chengdu. BociMed offers small-molecule chemistry, CMC and process development, a portfolio of drug delivery technology platforms (oral, injectable, nasal, pulmonary, transdermal, ocular, implant, liposome and exosome), clinical research and SMO services, global regulatory registration consulting, and commercial API, intermediate and solid-dosage manufacturing. It is a laboratory and manufacturing services business rather than a software vendor: it publishes a marketing website in Chinese and English and no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Hummingbird Bioscience
providers.description: Hummingbird Bioscience is a clinical-stage precision biotherapeutics company headquartered at The Galen, Singapore Science Park, with US operations, discovering and developing antibody-based medicines — including next-generation antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) — for hard-to-treat cancers and autoimmune disease. Its Rational Antibody Discovery (RAD) platform pairs computational target and epitope modelling with proprietary immunization strategies and Abvantage mice, and is combined with in-house linker-payload chemistry to engineer epitope-specific, high-affinity antibodies. Clinical programs include HMBD-001 (anti-HER3 monoclonal antibody) and HMBD-501 (HER3-targeted ADC, first patient dosed January 2026); HMBD-002 (anti-VISTA) was licensed to Percheron Therapeutics in 2025 and further antibodies were licensed to Immunome. The company sells drug programs and partnerships, not software: it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Ansa Biotechnologies
providers.description: Ansa Biotechnologies is a synthetic DNA manufacturer headquartered in Emeryville, California, founded in 2017 as a UC Berkeley spinout. Its enzymatic DNA synthesis platform is built on TdT-dNTP conjugates — enzymatic reagents that add single bases to a growing DNA molecule — and is sold as a made-to-order laboratory service producing sequence-verified double-stranded DNA fragments up to 600 bp, clonal DNA up to 7.5 kb, and ultra-long clonal constructs up to 50 kb. Quotes and orders are placed through a Salesforce Experience Cloud customer portal at portal.ansabio.com. Ansa is a wet-lab manufacturer rather than a software company: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Auransa
providers.description: Auransa Inc. is a clinical-stage, AI-native biopharmaceutical company based in Palo Alto, California, founded in 2014 by Pek Lum. Auransa uses its proprietary SMarTR Engine — a hypothesis-free machine learning platform that mines human disease data such as RNA transcriptome and gene-expression profiles — to discover novel small-molecule therapeutics without starting from a predefined drug target. The company has analyzed more than 500,000 gene-expression profiles across roughly 70 diseases to identify molecular disease subtypes and match them to candidate compounds. Its lead program, AU-409, is a first-in-human Phase 1 candidate for liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma), with additional pipeline work in heart-safe chemotherapy and other oncology indications. Auransa is a DCVC / DCVC Bio portfolio company, also backed by Lux Capital, 11.2 Capital, and Harmonix Fund. Auransa is a private drug-discovery company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its identity and web presence in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Cellanome
providers.description: Cellanome is a life-sciences technology company building multimodal single-cell analysis instrumentation. Its R3200 Platform combines live-cell imaging with single-cell transcriptomics using proprietary CellCage technology to isolate, observe, and perturb individual cells and track their dynamics over time, with applications across neurobiology, immunology, cancer research, aging, and CRISPR screening. Cellanome is venture-backed (8vc, DCVC, General Catalyst, SV Angel, Wing Venture Capital) and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and scientific-resources website but no public developer, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: EpiBiologics
providers.description: EpiBiologics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in San Mateo, California, developing bispecific antibodies for directed extracellular protein degradation. Its proprietary EpiTAC platform leverages an atlas of 270+ degradation-inducing cell-surface receptors to build tissue-selective therapies that degrade disease-causing proteins while sparing healthy tissue, targeting cancer, autoimmune, and other serious diseases. The company dosed its first patient with EPI-326 (an EGFR-driven solid-tumor bispecific) in a Phase 1 study in April 2026 and closed a $107M Series B round in January 2026. Backed by GV, EpiBiologics was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead profile; it publishes a corporate website but no public developer/API surface.

providers.name: Ndata
providers.description: nData (ndata.cz) is a European pharmaceutical software company operating since 2005 that builds GxP-compliant, AI-assisted systems for the pharma lifecycle: portfolio and project management (ePM), regulatory affairs (eRA), quality control planning (eQCP), artwork and packaging management (eAW), controlled documentation (eDOCS), clinical trial documentation / eTMF, plus eLAB (R&D lab operations), and eGO and eTRANSFER (launching Q3/2026). Its public web presence is a marketing and product-catalog site; nData publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specifications. Note: this repo was seeded as a bain-capital-ventures ai-infrastructure portfolio stub, but the ndata.cz surface is a pharmaceutical GxP software vendor — the portfolio match appears to be a mismatch.

providers.name: Panacea
providers.description: Panacea is an AI-native FDA regulatory services firm (Y Combinator Spring 2026, operating as withpanacea.com) that pairs experienced ex-FDA regulatory consultants with a proprietary AI platform to accelerate medical device and pharmaceutical companies through FDA approval. Panacea supports the full range of U.S. regulatory pathways - 510(k), De Novo, PMA, IDE, IND, NDA, BLA, ODD, Pre-Subs, and BDD - handling regulatory strategy, pre-FDA meetings, and submission authoring through to clearance and approval. The company differentiates on milestone-based, outcome-aligned pricing rather than hourly billing, claiming results roughly 60% faster than traditional firms while keeping 100% expert oversight. Panacea is a professional services / consulting company; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Mendel AI
providers.description: Mendel AI is a San Jose, California clinical AI company founded in 2017 by Dr. Karim Galil to streamline oncology research by organizing real-world data and accelerating clinical-trial workflows. Its flagship platform, Mendel Hypercube, pairs large language models with a clinician-built clinical knowledge hypergraph to add physician-like reasoning to LLMs operating over electronic health records, pathology reports, genomic data, clinician notes, claims, diagnostic data, and EDC submissions. Hypercube is offered as three productized experiences — Hypercube Cohort for patient cohort discovery (with funnel-style criteria analysis and direct integration to clinicaltrials.gov), Hypercube Analyst for AI-driven analysis of structured and unstructured real-world data, and Build Your Own Hypercube for custom clinical-data queries. The platform integrates with enterprise data warehouses (Databricks, Snowflake) and BI tools (Tableau, Qlik), and is available through the AWS Marketplace, Microsoft Azure Marketplace, and natively on the Snowflake AI Data Cloud. Mendel serves pharma, providers, payers, and research organizations including Quest Diagnostics, Boston Scientific, Gatehouse Bio, and the University of Pennsylvania, with published evidence in oncology trial prescreening. Mendel has no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open-source GitHub repositories; integration is delivered through enterprise contracts and cloud-marketplace deployments.

providers.name: Relay Therapeutics
providers.description: Relay Therapeutics is a clinical-stage precision-medicine company in Cambridge, Massachusetts that discovers and develops small-molecule therapeutics for cancer and genetic disease. Its proprietary Dynamo platform combines computational and experimental approaches — motion-based drug discovery, protein-motion simulation, structural biology, and biophysics — to drug targets that have historically been difficult to reach. The company advances a pipeline of oncology and precision-medicine candidates. Relay Therapeutics was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network. As a biotechnology / drug-discovery company it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; this profile captures its corporate identity and web properties.

providers.name: Allorion Therapeutics
providers.description: Allorion Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2020 by Qiang Ding and Fang Li, developing novel small-molecule therapies for cancer and autoimmune disease. Operating from Natick, Massachusetts and Guangzhou, China, Allorion applies mutant-selective and isoform-specific medicinal chemistry across a pipeline that includes ARTS-011 (a TYK2 inhibitor), ARTS-021 (a CDK2 inhibitor targeting CCNE1-amplified tumors), and ARTS-023/AVZO-023 partnered with Avenzo Therapeutics, alongside an exclusive option and global license agreement with AstraZeneca for an allosteric EGFR L858R inhibitor. The company is a drug-discovery organization backed by Qiming Venture Partners and INCE Capital; it markets internal data and high-throughput screening platforms but publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Amber Bio
providers.description: Amber Bio is a San Francisco-based biotechnology company founded in 2021 that is pioneering RNA-based gene editing. Its multi-kilobase RNA writing platform is designed to correct thousands of diverse mutations across a patient population with a single product, rather than requiring an independent therapy for each separate mutation. The company positions the approach as safe (minimal off-target effects), reversible, and capable of edits far larger than conventional base or prime editing, targeting previously undruggable genetic disease populations. Amber Bio launched publicly in August 2023 with an oversubscribed $26M seed round co-led by Playground Global and Andreessen Horowitz Bio + Health. It is a pre-clinical therapeutics company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Arzeda
providers.description: Arzeda Corp is a Seattle, Washington protein design company — "The Protein Design Company" — founded in 2008 by David Baker (2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry), Alexandre Zanghellini and colleagues out of the University of Washington Institute for Protein Design. Its Intelligent Protein Design Technology combines physics-based computational protein design, generative AI and an agentic design-build-test-learn loop over fifteen years of proprietary in-house experimental data to create designer enzymes and proteins that do not exist in nature, then scale them to commercial production. Commercial programs span food and beverage (ViaLeaf Reb M / ProSweet Reb M stevia sweeteners with MANE), home and personal care enzymes (Unilever), advanced materials (W. L. Gore & Associates) and pharmaceutical biologics (Takeda), alongside DARPA and NSF funded work on AI-driven protein design and cell-free biomanufacturing. Arzeda co-founded the OpenFold consortium for open-source protein structure prediction. It sells designed molecules and joint development programs, not software, and publishes no public developer program, API or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: AusperBio
providers.description: AusperBio — AusperBio Therapeutics, Inc. in the United States and Ausper Biopharma Co., Ltd. (杭州浩博医药有限公司) in Hangzhou, China — is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2019 that develops oligonucleotide and targeted delivery technologies, with an initial focus on achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B infection. Its proprietary Med-Oligo antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) platform pairs novel ASO design and optimization with targeted delivery conjugation chemistry, and its Au-HALO hepatocyte-targeting delivery technology extends the same modular approach to siRNA. The lead candidate AHB-137 is an unconjugated ASO that completed enrollment in two Phase II trials and received China CDE clearance to enter Phase III; a second clinical candidate, AHB-171, is a hepatocyte-targeted siRNA. The company has raised more than $200M across Series B, B+ and B2 rounds from investors including Qiming Venture Partners, HanKang Capital, CDH Investments, Sherpa Capital, YuanBio Venture Capital and Genesis Capital. AusperBio sells therapeutics, not software: it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract. Its only machine-readable surface is the private Spring Boot CMS backend that renders ausperbio.com, whose springdoc API description is correctly locked behind authentication.

providers.name: Avicenna Biosciences
providers.description: Avicenna Biosciences, Inc. is a Durham, North Carolina drug development company using machine learning-enhanced medicinal chemistry to accelerate the lead-to-candidate optimization process for small molecule drug development. Founded in 2020 and led by president and CEO Chris Meldrum, the company applies computational screening of candidate molecules for drug-like properties to the "last mile" of small molecule discovery, targeting neurodegenerative disease programs including Rho kinase inhibitors for Parkinson's disease and ALS. Avicenna raised a seed round led by DCVC Bio and has signed research collaborations with partners such as Molecure S.A. The company publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable interface as of this enrichment pass; it is catalogued here as an AI-for-drug-discovery company profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Basecamp Research
providers.description: Basecamp Research is a London-based biotech company mapping global genetic biodiversity to power AI-based design of biological systems. Its core asset is BaseGraph, a Neo4j-backed knowledge graph of billions of biological relationships assembled from novel protein and genome sequences collected under access-and-benefit-sharing partnerships with biodiversity-rich countries. On top of this data it builds foundation models and tools including EDEN (a large-scale biology sequence model), BaseFold (3D protein structure prediction that improves on AlphaFold2 for large, complex structures and small-molecule interactions), and BaseScan (an automated annotation pipeline). Basecamp works with pharma and biotech partners on drug discovery and enzyme/protein design, and has collaborated with NVIDIA to bring BaseFold to the BioNeMo platform. Backed by True Ventures. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Basecamp Research currently exposes no public self-serve developer API - data and models are accessed via partnerships, and product docs sit behind an authenticated portal.

providers.name: BigHat Biosciences
providers.description: BigHat Biosciences is a biotechnology company that pairs machine learning with a high-throughput, fully integrated wet lab to design next-generation antibody-based therapeutics. Its platform closes the loop between in-silico antibody design and in-house synthesis and characterization, generating proprietary experimental data that trains its models and speeds the discovery of biologics with improved developability. The company has publicly discussed its Reccy antibody design studio (RADS) and has entered machine-learning-enabled biologics collaborations with Eli Lilly (including Lilly TuneLab), Johnson & Johnson, and Lonza/Synaffix. BigHat is a private, venture-backed company (8VC, a16z) and maintains a public GitHub organization of open-source computational-biology tooling. It does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Cirius Therapeutics
providers.description: Cirius Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held clinical-stage pharmaceutical company based in Grand Rapids, Michigan, developing oral therapies for chronic metabolic diseases driven by insulin resistance, including Type 2 Diabetes, Type 1 Diabetes, obesity and gestational diabetes. Its lead candidate, azemiglitazone (CIR-0602K / MSDC-0602K), is a next-generation insulin sensitizer that inhibits the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC) to re-balance mitochondrial metabolism, improve glycemic control, preserve lean muscle mass and shift visceral fat to subcutaneous and brown adipose tissue, including in combination with GLP-1 receptor agonists such as tirzepatide. The company publishes a corporate marketing website only; it operates no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Element Science
providers.description: Element Science is a San Francisco-based medical device and digital health company focused on high-risk cardiovascular patients. Its flagship product is the Jewel Patch-Wearable Cardioverter Defibrillator (P-WCD) — a low-profile, water-resistant wearable that continuously monitors for and treats life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias in patients at temporary elevated risk of sudden cardiac arrest. The Jewel received FDA Premarket Approval in 2025 and CE Mark / UKCA marking in January 2024. Element Science is a portfolio company of GV. Added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; no public developer API or machine-readable specification has been identified for this provider at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Isomorphic Labs
providers.description: Isomorphic Labs is a London-based AI-first drug discovery company spun out of Google DeepMind in 2021 and operating as an Alphabet subsidiary. Founded and led by Sir Demis Hassabis, the company applies frontier AI — including derivatives of the Nobel-winning AlphaFold system and its proprietary Unified Drug Design Engine — to accelerate the design of small-molecule and biologic therapeutics across oncology, immunology, and other therapeutic areas. The Drug Design Engine is positioned as a target- and disease-agnostic, multi-modality platform that combines predictive and generative models with a curated proprietary life-science "Dataverse" and large-scale GPU infrastructure. Isomorphic Labs monetises through strategic pharmaceutical research collaborations — disclosed deals include Novartis (January 2024, expanded February 2025), Eli Lilly, and Johnson & Johnson (January 2026) — and through its own internal therapeutic pipeline. The company closed a $600M external Series B investment round in March 2025. Isomorphic Labs does not operate a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release of its Drug Design Engine; external researcher access to AlphaFold-family models is provided separately by Google DeepMind via the free AlphaFold Server (alphafoldserver.com) for non-commercial use, and via the open-source AlphaFold 3 inference code released by DeepMind. The Isomorphic Labs GitHub organisation hosts only a small number of forks of internal Kubernetes and configuration-management tooling.

providers.name: Liberate Bio
providers.description: Liberate Bio is a genetic medicine company developing in vivo cell therapies that reach cell populations beyond the liver, the long-standing limit of lipid nanoparticle delivery. Its RAPTOR discovery platform is a scalable in vivo screening system that identifies LNP delivery vehicles which work with existing biology to carry genetic payloads into immune cells in blood, bone marrow, and the spleen. Liberate Bio applies that delivery capability to in vivo CAR-M (chimeric antigen receptor macrophage) programs, reprogramming monocytes and macrophages to eliminate disease-driving cells without ex vivo manipulation, with programs in hematologic oncology and in autoimmune disease via depletion of pathogenic B-cell populations. Founded by Nessan Bermingham, Theresa M. Reineke, and Michael Mitchell, and led by CEO Shawn Davis and CSO Walter Strapps, the company raised $31M from Khosla Ventures in October 2025. It is pre-clinical and publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: OrsoBio
providers.description: OrsoBio is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2021 and headquartered in Palo Alto, California, developing first-in-class oral therapies that restore energy homeostasis in patients living with severe metabolic disorders — obesity, type 2 diabetes, severe dyslipidemias, lipodystrophies and MASH. The name is drawn from the metabolic adaptability of bears ("orso" in Italian). Its pipeline is led by three mitochondrial protonophores — TLC-6740, TLC-1180 and TLC-1235 — intended to increase energy expenditure and improve metabolic and cardiovascular health, alongside an LXR inverse agonist (TLC-2716) for severe hypertriglyceridemia and MASH, an ACC2 inhibitor (TLC-3595) for insulin sensitivity in type 2 diabetes, and an ACMSD inhibitor to augment NAD+ biosynthesis in metabolic and inflammatory liver and kidney disorders. The company closed an oversubscribed $67 million Series B in September 2024, co-led by Ascenta Capital and Woodline Partners with participation from Samsara BioCapital, Enavate Sciences and Longitude Capital. OrsoBio publishes a corporate site covering its science, pipeline, team, board, publications, events and press releases, but runs no developer program: no API documentation, no SDKs, no developer portal, no GitHub organisation and no machine-readable API contract of any kind. The only machine-readable surface on orsobio.com is the site's own WordPress CMS route index, which the site's robots.txt explicitly disallows at /wp-json/ and which is therefore not harvested or catalogued here.

providers.name: uncommonbio
providers.description: Uncommon (uncommonbio.co, formerly Higher Steaks) is a Cambridge, UK biotechnology company backed by Balderton Capital. The company sold its cultivated meat platform to Vow and has pivoted to launch SymphoRNA, a new venture developing nucleic acid delivery technology for multi-RNA combination medicines that target complex diseases such as fibrosis, heart failure, and neurodegeneration. As a life-sciences research and platform company, Uncommon publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API specification. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of Balderton Capital and enriched via the local enrichment pipeline, which confirmed the absence of an API surface while capturing live domain-security posture.

providers.name: Asymchem
providers.description: Asymchem (Asymchem Laboratories (Tianjin) Co., Ltd.) is a global contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) with more than 25 years of experience delivering integrated, cGMP-compliant services across the pharmaceutical value chain. Its single-source model spans route scouting, process research and development, scale-up, and commercial manufacturing for small molecules, peptides, oligonucleotides, chemical macromolecules, biologics, and synthetic biology, and is known for green chemistry and continuous flow chemistry. Headquartered in Morrisville, North Carolina with major R&D and manufacturing operations in China, the U.S., and the U.K., Asymchem employs roughly 9,000 people and is publicly listed (002821.SZ / 6821.HK). Surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan and added to the API Evangelist network. Note: "API" in Asymchem's context refers to Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient manufacturing, not a public web/developer API — the company publishes no developer API surface.

providers.name: Nouscom
providers.description: Nouscom AG is a private, clinical-stage immuno-oncology company developing next-generation neoantigen-targeted cancer immunotherapies, founded in 2015 by Riccardo Cortese and Alfredo Nicosia, with headquarters in Basel, Switzerland and research and manufacturing operations in Rome, Italy. Its proprietary viral vector platform — great ape adenovirus and MVA vectors able to encode large neoantigen payloads together with other immunomodulators — is used to build both off-the-shelf and personalized cancer vaccines. The lead program, NOUS-209, targets 209 shared frameshift neoantigens for cancer interception in Lynch Syndrome carriers and for the treatment of dMMR/MSI metastatic colorectal cancer in combination with pembrolizumab; its second clinical program, NOUS-PEV, is a personalized immunotherapy for advanced solid tumors. Nouscom raised an oversubscribed EUR 67.5 million Series C in November 2023, co-led by Andera Partners, Bpifrance (InnoBio 2) and M Ventures. Nouscom is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable API contract, and is profiled here as an identity-only record.

providers.name: Sherlock Biosciences
providers.description: Sherlock Biosciences is a molecular diagnostics company founded in 2019 out of the Broad Institute to commercialize SHERLOCK (Specific High-sensitivity Enzymatic Reporter unLOCKing), the CRISPR-based nucleic-acid detection method developed in the Zhang lab, alongside INSPECTR, an ambient-temperature synthetic-biology amplification platform.
