In May 2020 it received the first FDA Emergency Use Authorization ever granted to a CRISPR-based diagnostic, for SARS-CoV-2. The company developed disposable, instrument-free molecular self-tests, led by a combined Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae assay. OraSure Technologies acquired Sherlock Biosciences in December 2024 and absorbed it into its rapid-diagnostics portfolio; the sherlock.bio domain now permanently redirects to orasure.com. Sherlock Biosciences is a laboratory diagnostics developer and has never operated a public developer program, HTTP API, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: XtalPi
providers.description: XtalPi is an AI-and-quantum-physics drug discovery and materials research platform company with headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts and major operations in Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen, publicly listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under stock code 2228.HK. The company combines a hybrid AI plus quantum mechanics (QM) discovery engine with large-scale robotic laboratory automation to accelerate molecular research and development for pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials customers, including engagements with Pfizer, Eli Lilly, and Novartis. XtalPi's offering spans proprietary software platforms — PatSight for patent extraction, XFEP for free-energy perturbation binding-affinity prediction, XMolGen for generative chemistry, and XtalGazer for solid-state research — and intelligent automation hardware including the XmartChem intelligent synthesis workstation and ChemPlus desktop solid dispenser. Its drug discovery services cover hit discovery, hit/lead optimization, biology capabilities, focused library synthesis, and the PepiX peptide platform, complemented by sister brands Ailux (biology) and AiFChem (chemistry). XtalPi's products are delivered as enterprise collaborations, licensed software, and CRO-style services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release.

providers.name: Saul Ewing LLP
providers.description: Saul Ewing LLP is a U.S.-based law firm founded in 1921 as Saul, Ewing, Remick & Saul, with more than 450 attorneys across 17 U.S. offices spanning the Mid-Atlantic, Northeast, Midwest, Florida, and California. The firm serves clients across 40+ industries with practice strengths in litigation, corporate and M&A, bankruptcy and restructuring, real estate, public finance, life sciences, financial services, intellectual property, labor and employment, and cybersecurity and privacy. Saul Ewing does not publish a public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or machine-readable data product; its public technology surface is limited to its corporate website, a HighQ-powered client portal, the SEquel Alumni Portal at alumni.saul.com, employee remote-access tooling, and a small set of practice-specific blogs (Construction Industry Counselor, OZ and EB-5 Investments, Legacy Matters, The Friday Five). Two empty GitHub organizations (Saul-Ewing and saulewing) exist with zero public repositories.

providers.name: Akston Biosciences
providers.description: Akston Biosciences Corporation is a privately held biotechnology company headquartered in Beverly, Massachusetts, founded in 2011 by the team from SmartCells, Inc. and led by CEO Todd Zion, Ph.D. Akston designs, develops and manufactures protein therapeutics built on its proprietary Ambifect Fc-fusion protein platform, with a pipeline focused on companion-animal (veterinary) medicine: PD-L1 monoclonal antibody oncology candidates (AKS-701d, AKS-619d), a long-acting GLP-1 for feline weight management (AKS-562c), an IL-31 targeting therapy for canine pruritus (AKS-699), and NGF-targeting candidates for osteoarthritis pain. Its veterinary insulin program was sold to Dechra in 2024, and human programs continue through the Vakston and Diamune Therapeutics subsidiaries. The company announced a manufacturing expansion in Shreveport, Louisiana. Akston is a therapeutics developer and manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes a corporate marketing site and no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Alume Biosciences
providers.description: Alume Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company in La Jolla, California, developing nerve-targeted fluorescent agents for precision surgery. Its lead candidate, bevonescein (ALM-488) — a peptide-dye conjugate co-invented by the late Nobel Laureate Dr. Roger Tsien and surgeon Dr. Quyen Nguyen — is administered intravenously roughly an hour before an operation so surgeons can see nerves illuminated in the surgical field and avoid inadvertent nerve injury. The compound has FDA Fast Track designation, is in Phase 3 pivotal trials in head-and-neck surgery, and the company has stated it plans a New Drug Application submission in 2026. Alume is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Antiva Biosciences
providers.description: Antiva Biosciences is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing topical therapeutics that target oncogenic human papillomavirus (HPV) infections and the precancerous cervical lesions they cause, aiming to stop cervical cancer before it starts with at-home, non-surgical treatment. Its lead candidate, ABI-2280, is a topical antiviral in Phase 1b/2 clinical development for high-risk cervical HPV infection, and the company frames its work in support of the World Health Organization's global Cervical Cancer Elimination Initiative. Antiva is backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners and GV, and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile awaiting further enrichment.

providers.name: Atlas Discovery
providers.description: Atlas Discovery is an AI-powered biotechnology company (Y Combinator Summer 2026) building foundation models of human patient biology to predict how people will respond to drugs in clinical trials. Nine of ten drugs fail in trials because no animal model or cell in a dish reliably predicts a human response; Atlas Discovery trains models on preclinical and clinical data to improve trial design and rescue stalled drug programs. Its research spans single-cell representation learning (ExpressionVAE) and clinical response prediction, with work presented at ICLR '26, ICML '26, and CSHL '26. The company is an early-stage research lab with no public API, developer program, or product surface yet; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead awaiting a public developer offering.

providers.name: Cullgen
providers.description: Cullgen Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 2018 and focused on first-in-class targeted protein degradation medicines. Its proprietary uSMITE (ubiquitin-mediated, small molecule-induced target elimination) platform harnesses the body's own ubiquitin-proteasome system to selectively degrade disease-causing intracellular proteins, including targets considered undruggable by conventional small molecules, and the company extends that chemistry into degrader-antibody conjugates (DACs). Its lead TRK degrader program has entered Phase 1 clinical dosing, and the company has partnered with Astellas and taken investment from AstraZeneca. Gyre Therapeutics completed an all-stock acquisition of Cullgen valued at approximately $300 million on 4 May 2026. Cullgen publishes a corporate marketing website only: profiling on 2026-08-04 found no developer portal, documentation, machine-readable API contract, package registry presence, or public code repositories.

providers.name: DeepCell
providers.description: Deepcell is a Menlo Park, California life-sciences company building an AI-powered platform for label-free single-cell morphology analysis, a field it calls morpholomics. Its REM-I platform combines label-free imaging, deep learning, and gentle cell enrichment to treat single-cell morphology as a high-dimensional, quantitative biological readout without destructive sample preparation. Applications span oncology and tumor heterogeneity profiling, phenotypic drug discovery, cell and gene therapy quality control and manufacturing, regenerative medicine, transplant monitoring, neurobiology, and agriculture. Backed by a16z and DCVC, Deepcell was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; it currently publishes a corporate site, blog, and publications but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Dizal Pharma
providers.description: Dizal Pharma (Dizal (Jiangsu) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on discovering and developing novel medicines in oncology and immunology. Originating in 2017 from research capabilities established in China, the company operates research and development across Shanghai and Wuxi (Jiangsu), China, and is listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market (ticker 688192). Dizal's most advanced programs include sunvozertinib (DZD9008), an oral EGFR exon 20 insertion inhibitor for non-small cell lung cancer marketed as Zegfrovy, and golidocitinib (DZD4205), a selective JAK1 inhibitor developed for relapsed/refractory peripheral T-cell lymphoma. Dizal Pharma was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm HongShan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). As a pharmaceutical developer it publishes a corporate marketing and investor-facing website but does not expose a public developer platform, API program, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time; this profile captures the company identity for the network.

providers.name: Elektrofi
providers.description: Elektrofi is a Boston-based biopharmaceutical formulation technology company reinventing how biologic therapies are delivered to patients. Its Hypercon ultra-high-concentration microparticle platform and Elektroject process turn monoclonal antibodies, therapeutic proteins, and other large-molecule drugs into stable, syringe-injectable formulations suited to small-volume, at-home subcutaneous self-administration instead of intravenous infusion. The company has partnered with Eli Lilly and Janssen Biotech (Johnson & Johnson) on multi-target drug-delivery collaborations, and was acquired by Halozyme Therapeutics in November 2025. Elektrofi is a biotechnology company and does not publish a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company entity within the network.

providers.name: Gate Bioscience
providers.description: Gate Bioscience is a preclinical biotechnology company founded in 2021 and headquartered in Brisbane, California, creating a new class of small-molecule medicines called Molecular Gates. Molecular Gates selectively eliminate disease-causing extracellular proteins at their origin inside the cell by binding the secretory translocon, the channel through which proteins exit the cell, so targeted proteins are degraded rather than secreted. The company's proprietary Molecular Gate Discovery Platform pairs a privileged library of molecules with bespoke secretion-focused assays and deep secretory-pathway biology to pursue more than 1,000 diseases linked to extracellular proteins. Gate Bioscience is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) Bio + Health, GV, Versant Ventures, ARCH Venture Partners, Forbion and Eli Lilly, and has raised roughly $134M across Series A and an oversubscribed $65M Series B. As a therapeutics company it publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation; this profile is an API Evangelist network company record maintained for the portfolio graph.

providers.name: M20 Genomics
providers.description: M20 Genomics is a life-science technology company advancing single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. Its VITA platform delivers single-cell full-length transcriptome sequencing across sample types and species, supported by the VITAcruizer single-cell partitioning system, VITApilote library-preparation kits, and VITAseer bioinformatics software. The company's M20 Seq and M20 Spatial technologies serve basic research (cancer, neurobiology, immunology, developmental biology), clinical research (oncology, reproductive medicine, infectious diseases), and drug development and target screening, including prokaryotic and eukaryotic single-cell RNA sequencing. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes lab instruments, reagent kits, and analysis software rather than a public web API or developer platform.

providers.name: Medra
providers.description: Medra builds an AI-powered robotic platform for autonomous laboratory work in the life sciences. Its "Physical AI Scientist" combines robotic hardware, computer vision, and scientific reasoning AI to design, execute, and continuously optimize experiments — gene editing, RNA/nucleic-acid work, antibody design, and cell-based assays — the way a human scientist would. Units are deployed at partner sites including Genentech and Addition Therapeutics, with a DARPA collaboration on its AI Experimentalist reasoning layer. Founded by Michelle Lee and headquartered in San Francisco, Medra raised a $52M Series A (Dec 2025) from investors including Lux Capital and Menlo Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Medra publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Monte Rosa Therapeutics *
providers.description: Monte Rosa Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering molecular glue degrader (MGD) medicines. It pairs its QuEEN discovery engine — integrating artificial intelligence, machine learning, and structural biology — with proprietary chemistry to design small molecules that selectively degrade disease-causing proteins previously considered undruggable, across oncology and immunology, with collaborations including Novartis and Roche. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation; this profile captures its web presence and probed domain-security surface.

providers.name: OMass Therapeutics
providers.description: OMass Therapeutics is an Oxford, UK biotechnology company developing medicines for immunological and rare diseases. It harnesses proprietary biochemistry, native mass spectrometry and custom chemistry through its OdyssION drug discovery platform to interrogate drug targets and how they interact with their native biological ecosystem, separate from the confounding complexity of the cell. The company operates a corporate and scientific web presence (science, pipeline, publications, news and blog) and, as a therapeutics company, publishes no public developer or API surface. Backed by GV and other life-sciences investors.

providers.name: Ouro Medicines
providers.description: Ouro Medicines is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in South San Francisco, California, defining the future of treatment for people with immune-mediated diseases. Its pipeline centers on T cell engager programs for autoimmune conditions, including the lead candidate OM336 (evaluated in the AIC-1001 clinical trial), alongside an expanded access policy. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead. As a therapeutics developer, Ouro Medicines publishes a corporate and scientific website but no public developer program, API, or technical documentation surface. Recent company news includes a definitive agreement for Gilead Sciences to acquire Ouro Medicines to advance its first-in-class T cell engager program for autoimmune diseases.

providers.name: Somite
providers.description: Somite (now operating as Cellular Intelligence) is an AI-native TechBio company backed by Khosla Ventures building a universal virtual cell-signaling foundation model to engineer cellular fate. In 2026 the company rebranded from Somite to Cellular Intelligence and entered an agreement with Novo Nordisk to advance STEM-PD, a clinical-stage cell therapy for Parkinson's disease that carries FDA Fast Track Designation. The company works at the intersection of machine learning and regenerative medicine and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or other machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Ventus Therapeutics
providers.description: Ventus Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on small-molecule drug discovery for biologically validated targets historically considered undruggable, across inflammatory, immunological, cardiometabolic, and neurological diseases. Its ReSOLVE platform combines AI/ML, protein science, structural biology, and biophysics to accelerate discovery; the pipeline includes VENT-03 (cGAS inhibitor), VENT-02 (NLRP3 inhibitor), and VENT-04 (caspase-4/5 inhibitor). Headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts with a site in Saint-Laurent, Quebec, and backed by GV and the SoftBank Vision Fund. The company operates no public developer API surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record.

providers.name: Virtuoso Therapeutics
providers.description: Virtuoso Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company advancing a pipeline of novel bispecific antibodies to treat cancer. Using a differentiated approach to antibody engineering, the company designs molecules intended to overcome the limitations of existing therapies and to address major hurdles facing emerging classes of oncology treatments. Virtuoso is a venture-backed portfolio company of Canaan Partners. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; the company currently publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Be Biopharma
providers.description: Be Biopharma (Be Bio) is a Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company founded in October 2020 by Longwood Fund together with B cell engineering researchers David Rawlings, M.D. and Richard James, Ph.D. of Seattle Children's Research Institute. The company develops engineered B Cell Medicines (BCMs) — a patient's own B cells engineered to produce a therapeutic protein — for genetic disease, cancer and other serious conditions. Its lead candidate, BE-101, inserted a functional Factor IX gene into primary human B cells for hemophilia B and held FDA Orphan Drug and Fast Track designations; a second program, BE-102, targeted hypophosphatasia. The company raised $82M in October 2024 and $92M in a January 2025 Series C, dosed the first participant in the Phase 1/2 BeCoMe-9 trial in July 2025, and terminated that trial in June 2026 for stated strategic business reasons. Be Biopharma is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it has never published a developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Denali Therapeutics
providers.description: Denali Therapeutics is a South San Francisco-based biopharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, and delivers therapeutics for people living with serious neurodegenerative and lysosomal storage diseases. Its proprietary Transport Vehicle (TV) platform is engineered to cross the blood-brain barrier so that large-molecule therapies can reach the brain and body. Denali maintains a public GitHub organization publishing open-source computational-biology and cheminformatics research tools (archs4, basechem, napari-mito-hcs), but publishes no public developer API. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences portfolio company of GV.

providers.name: Elion Therapeutics
providers.description: Elion Therapeutics is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company developing treatments for life-threatening invasive fungal infections (IFIs). Formerly known as Sfunga Therapeutics, the company was founded on the belief that mechanistic insight into natural products enables targeted optimization of them. Its lead candidate, SF001, is a next-generation polyene antifungal — a rationally designed analog of amphotericin B intended to retain broad fungicidal activity while mitigating the systemic toxicity that limits the parent molecule. SF001 received FDA Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) and Fast Track designations in 2023 and has advanced from a first-in-human single-ascending-dose study into multiple-ascending-dose evaluation. Elion closed an $81 million Series B in June 2024 led by Deerfield Management and the AMR Action Fund, with participation from Illinois Ventures. Elion is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, public API, or machine-readable API contract, and this profile records that absence rather than any API surface.

providers.name: Initial Therapeutics
providers.description: Initial Therapeutics, Inc. is a preclinical-stage biotechnology company in South San Francisco, California, discovering and developing a new class of small-molecule medicines designed to halt pathogenic protein formation in its earliest stages. Its proprietary STOPS platform — Selective Termination of Protein Synthesis — intercepts the translation of a target protein inside the exit tunnel of the ribosome, recognizing the nascent primary linear sequence rather than a fully folded three-dimensional structure, an approach the company positions as starkly differentiated from targeted protein degradation and from interventions that can only act on proteins after they are fully formed. The company launched publicly on May 1, 2023 with a $75 million Series A from Apple Tree Partners, was co-founded with academic scientists Jamie H. D. Cate (UC Berkeley), Brian Paegel (UC Irvine) and Kevan Shokat (UCSF/UC Berkeley), and builds on ribosome biochemistry, proteomics, medicinal chemistry, DNA-encoded library technology and chemical genetics, with early programs aimed at oncology targets long considered undruggable. Initial Therapeutics is a therapeutics discovery company, not a software vendor: it publishes a small marketing website and no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: IQVIA
providers.description: IQVIA empowers life sciences organizations to accelerate innovation, improve patient outcomes, and bring treatments to market faster through advanced analytics and technology. IQVIA is a Fortune 500 company offering data, analytics, clinical research, and connected intelligence services.

providers.name: Novartis
providers.description: Novartis AG is a Swiss multinational pharmaceutical corporation headquartered in Basel, Switzerland, and one of the largest pharmaceutical companies in the world by revenue. The company focuses on innovative medicines across oncology, immunology, neuroscience, cardiovascular, renal, and metabolic disease areas. Novartis does not publish a public external developer API. The company does maintain an Open Source Science programme that releases scientific computing libraries, Drupal modules, and informatics tooling on GitHub for use by the research community.

providers.name: PerkinElmer
providers.description: PerkinElmer is a global leader in scientific instrumentation, lab services, and informatics for life sciences, diagnostics, food, environmental, and industrial markets. The company provides analytical instruments, reagents, software, and software downloads to support laboratory operations and scientific research.

providers.name: Pharmazz
providers.description: Pharmazz, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Willowbrook, Illinois, founded and led by pharmacologist Dr. Anil Gulati. The company discovers, develops and commercializes first-in-class therapeutics for critical care and neurovascular medicine, built around two lead small-molecule candidates: centhaquine (Lyfaquin), a resuscitative agent for hypovolemic shock that holds marketing authorization from the Drugs Controller General of India and is licensed to Dr. Reddy's Laboratories for the Indian market, and sovateltide (Tycamzzi), an endothelin-B receptor agonist for cerebral ischemic stroke. Additional pipeline programs target septic shock, acute kidney injury, cardiac arrest, acute spinal cord injury, hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy and Alzheimer's disease. Pharmazz is a drug-development company, not a software vendor; its public web presence is a corporate and investor brochure site and it operates no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Quintiles Transnational Holdings
providers.description: Quintiles Transnational Holdings was a Fortune 500 contract research organization (CRO) that provided biopharmaceutical development and commercial outsourcing services to the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device industries. In October 2016, Quintiles merged with IMS Health to form IQVIA, a leading provider of advanced analytics, technology solutions, and contract research services to the life sciences industry. The legacy Quintiles entity no longer operates as an independent company and does not maintain a public API program; all developer-facing capabilities are now part of IQVIA.

providers.name: Scorpion Therapeutics
providers.description: Scorpion Therapeutics is a clinical-stage precision oncology biotechnology company founded in 2020 and headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts. It pursued what it called Precision Oncology 2.0 — integrating target discovery, medicinal chemistry and translational medicine to produce mutant-selective small-molecule cancer drugs — led by STX-478, an oral mutant-selective PI3K-alpha inhibitor in Phase 1/2 trials for breast cancer and other advanced solid tumors, and STX-721, a covalent EGFR/HER2 exon 20 inhibitor. In January 2025 Eli Lilly agreed to acquire Scorpion and its PI3K-alpha program in a transaction valued at up to $2.5 billion, with the non-PI3K-alpha pipeline and staff spun into a separate independent company. Scorpion is a drug developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification, and its own domain now redirects to the acquirer's announcement.

providers.name: Syapse
providers.description: Syapse was a San Francisco precision-medicine software company, founded in 2008, that built a real-world evidence platform for community oncology. Its product integrated structured clinical data from health-system EHRs with genomic/NGS results to support molecular tumor boards, care coordination, quality improvement and life-sciences research, and it ran the Syapse Learning Health Network of community health systems alongside collaborations with Roche, Amgen and the US Department of Veterans Affairs. Syapse Holdings was acquired by N-Power Medicine in a stock-for-stock exchange that closed 2024-12-30 and was announced 2025-01-12; its network of 1,000+ community oncologists, its data and technology stack, and its team were folded into N-Power Medicine's always-on community clinical-research model. The Syapse brand has since been fully retired: syapse.com now serves nothing but a 292-byte meta-refresh stub redirecting to npowermedicine.com, dated 2025-01-12. Syapse never published a public developer program, and no public API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, SDK or developer portal survives.

providers.name: Tearclear
providers.description: TearClear Corp. is a clinical-stage ophthalmic pharmaceutical company founded in 2015 that develops a preservative-removing drug delivery platform: a chemical filter built into a conventional multi-dose eye-drop bottle that captures benzalkonium chloride (BAK) at the point of instillation, so the medication stays preserved in the bottle but reaches the ocular surface preservative-free. Its lead candidate TC-002 (latanoprost ophthalmic solution 0.005%) met the primary and all secondary endpoints in the CLEAR Phase 3 pivotal glaucoma trial, with TC-001 (timolol), TC-003 (brimonidine/timolol) and TC-004 (brimonidine) behind it. TearClear ships drug products and delivery hardware, not software: it operates no developer program and publishes no API, SDK or machine-readable contract, and its own corporate domain no longer resolves to a served website.

providers.name: Allevi
providers.description: Allevi is a bioprinting company that designs and manufactures 3D bioprinters, bioinks, and accompanying software for tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, and life-sciences research. Its desktop bioprinters and biomaterials let researchers fabricate living tissue constructs for drug discovery, disease modeling, and organ-on-chip work. Allevi was acquired by 3D Systems and operates as part of its regenerative medicine portfolio. The company publishes bioprinting protocols, application notes, webinars, and white papers, but exposes no public web API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Rome Therapeutics
providers.description: Rome Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company developing therapies that target the "repeatome" — the vast repetitive, non-coding regions of the human genome (the "dark genome," including LINE-1 and other transposable elements) implicated in cancer and autoimmune disease. Its discovery engine pairs ROMEMap, a proprietary high-resolution database of annotated functional repeats, with ROMEQuant, a machine-learning method for quantifying repeat expression and prioritizing targets and biomarkers. Backed by a16z and GV, the company raised a $77M Series B (2021) plus a $72M Series B extension to advance its lead program into clinical development. These are internal research/data-science tools; the company publishes no public developer or web API. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: IDEXX Laboratories
providers.description: Profile for IDEXX Laboratories in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 887).

regulatory.note: provider carries no tags; regime could not be determined

providers.name: abbisko
providers.description: Abbisko Therapeutics (上海和誉生物医药科技有限公司) is a Shanghai-based clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery and development of innovative small-molecule therapeutics, primarily in oncology. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or agent surface — this is a biopharmaceutical R&D company, not an API provider — so no API artifacts apply; only a live domain-security probe was captured.

providers.name: Acceleron
providers.description: Acceleron is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: aceabio
providers.description: ACEA Biosciences (aceabio) is a life-sciences company known for cell-analysis instrumentation that was acquired by Agilent Technologies; its aceabio.com.cn domain now redirects to an Agilent landing page (explore.agilent.com/ACEA-joins-Agilent). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the Qiming venture firm and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no independent developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or public API surface for the standalone entity — the operating web presence has been folded into Agilent.

providers.name: aceatherapeutics
providers.description: ACEA Therapeutics (aceatherapeutics.com) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing innovative small-molecule and antibody-drug-conjugate treatments across oncology, autoimmune, and antiviral therapeutic areas, with product candidates including Olgotrelvir, Abivertinib, AC0058, STI-6129, and AC0939. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a pharmaceutical company oriented toward patients, physicians, and investors, ACEA Therapeutics publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or technical integration surface at this time; this profile captures its verifiable web/domain footprint only.

providers.name: Achira
providers.description: Achira is a digital-biology company building molecular world models to transform drug discovery and the physical sciences. Founded by John Chodera, Theofanis Karaletsos, and Zavain Dar, it blends geometric deep learning, generative AI, physics, quantum chemistry, and statistical mechanics into foundation simulation models that enable out-of-distribution prediction at the atomistic scale — a "third path" between pure machine-learning approaches and traditional molecular dynamics simulation. Achira raised a $33M Series A from Dimension, Amplify Partners, NVIDIA NVentures, and Compound. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: acxel
providers.description: ACXEL is a digital cell biology company building advanced microfluidics platforms and productivity tools for life sciences research and drug development. Its self-developed AP-LOC (Active Pixel Lab-on-Chip) technology enables high-throughput, parallel, and precise microdroplet manipulation, alongside AM-EWOD and AM-DMF digital microfluidic platforms supporting cell sorting, cell therapy, antibody therapy, synthetic biology, and chemical synthesis with full-process chip integration and real-time feedback monitoring. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. ACXEL is a hardware and platform provider and publishes no public developer/API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Allena Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Allena Pharmaceuticals is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Apollomics, Inc.
providers.description: Apollomics, Inc. (Nasdaq: APLM) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Foster City, California, focused on the discovery and development of oncology therapies designed to be combined with other treatments to harness the immune system and target specific molecular pathways that inhibit cancer. Operating since 2016, Apollomics has a pipeline of nine drug candidates spanning small-molecule targeted drugs and biologics, including late-stage programs such as vebreltinib (Phase 2, NSCLC and solid tumors with cMet dysregulation) and uproleselan (Phase 3 in China for relapsed/refractory AML). The company became publicly traded via a business combination with Maxpro Capital Acquisition Corp. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network; as a biopharmaceutical company it publishes no public developer API surface — this profile carries its corporate identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Arda Therapeutics
providers.description: Arda Therapeutics is a San Carlos, California biotech company founded in 2021 that develops targeted cell depletion therapies for chronic disease. Rather than modulating the proteins that pathogenic cells produce, Arda uses a single-cell sequencing and computational discovery engine to map disease-specific cell states, identify surface markers on harmful cells, and design targeted biologics that selectively deplete them across fibrotic, autoimmune, and metabolic conditions. Backed by a $43M Series A led by a16z Bio + Health with GV, Two Sigma Ventures, Eli Lilly and others. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer and web surface; Arda currently publishes a corporate marketing site with no public developer API.

providers.name: Areteia Therapeutics
providers.description: Areteia Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company, formerly based in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, operating in the life-sciences sector. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company is no longer operating: areteiatx.com serves only a closure notice directing asset and general inquiries to contact addresses, and the company publishes no developer portal, API, documentation, SDKs, or other technical developer surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of gv (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; retained for network completeness with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Aria Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Aria Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company that applies artificial intelligence and machine learning to drug discovery, using a computational platform to identify and advance small-molecule therapeutic candidates for complex, inflammatory, and immunological diseases. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Aria operates as a therapeutics developer rather than a software or API provider. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company profile; an enrichment pass found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or other programmatic developer surface for the company at this time.

providers.name: Arpelos Biosciences
providers.description: Arpelos Biosciences is a seed-stage biotechnology company based in Kendall Square, Cambridge, developing multivalent medicines — therapeutics engineered for high potency and selectivity by engaging multiple targets or sites simultaneously. The founding team comprises scientists from UCSF, Penn, Stanford, and MIT spanning computational biology, immunology, and protein engineering, and the company is backed by prominent biotech investors including Wing Venture Capital. Arpelos currently operates as a stealth-stage research company with a single-page web presence and does not publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company identity record awaiting any future developer surface.

providers.name: ArsenalBio
providers.description: ArsenalBio is a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company in South San Francisco developing programmable, integrated cell therapies for solid tumors. Its platform engineers autonomous CAR-T cells using large-scale genome engineering and computational biology to create multi-functional therapies. Backed by Kleiner Perkins and SoftBank Vision Fund, the company operates in the healthcare and biotechnology sector. It publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation; this profile is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record.

providers.name: Aspire Health *
providers.description: Aspire Health was a community-based palliative care provider surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences stub. The company delivered home- and clinic-based palliative and serious-illness care and was acquired by Anthem (now Elevance Health) in 2018; its aspirehealthcare.com domain today redirects into the Carelon Health / CareMore Health palliative-care service line. Aspire Health is a healthcare services organization, not a technology or API provider: enrichment found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. This profile is retained as a network lead with only the identity and domain-security posture that could be verified from public probes.

providers.name: atantares
providers.description: Atantares (芯宿科技) is a Chinese synthetic-biology company based in Suzhou Industrial Park that builds "silicon-based biology" — semiconductor-driven biotechnology. Its chip-based, high-throughput platform (the EcoSyn synthesizer and ECHOS MicroArray, using electrochemical oligonucleotide synthesis on CMOS/MEMS microelectrode arrays) drives low-cost, high-fidelity DNA synthesis and is expanding into RNA and protein synthesis and detection. Research-service offerings include primer/oligo synthesis, gene synthesis, gene sequencing, cloning and mutagenesis, strain-library preparation, and gene editing, built on an in-house full-workflow automation, sequence-analysis, and order-management platform. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners. The company operates a marketing website only and publishes no public developer program, API, or documentation at the time of this profile.

providers.name: Atara Bio
providers.description: Atara Biotherapeutics is a clinical-stage allogeneic (off-the-shelf) T-cell immunotherapy company developing transformative therapies that harness T cells to fight cancer and autoimmune conditions, and is the first company to receive regulatory approval for an allogeneic T-cell immunotherapy. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Kleiner Perkins and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes a corporate website but no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation was found; this profile carries identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Autolus *
providers.description: Autolus is a life-sciences (biopharmaceutical) company operating in the cell-therapy space, developing programmed / engineered T cell (CAR-T) therapies for cancer and other serious diseases. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a clinical/commercial-stage biopharma, its public web presence (autolus.com) is a corporate marketing and investor-relations site rather than a developer platform: no public API, developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI surface was found during enrichment. The only machine-discoverable artifact is a minimal RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: Aviceda Therapeutics
providers.description: Aviceda Therapeutics is a private, late-stage clinical biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts that describes itself as the world leader in glyco-immune checkpoint therapeutics. It develops immune-mediated therapies built on a glyco-mimetic nanoparticle platform that targets the interaction between sialic acids on cell surfaces and Siglec immune receptors in order to modulate aberrant inflammation. Its lead asset, AVD-104, is an intravitreally administered sialic-acid-coated nanoparticle being evaluated in the Phase 2/3 SIGLEC trial for geographic atrophy secondary to age-related macular degeneration. Aviceda is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Axcelius I/II
providers.description: Axcelius I/II is a biopharmaceutical company-creation vehicle backed by Canaan Partners, formed to found and incubate drug-development companies pursuing treatments for cancer, rare diseases, and neurodegenerative disorders. It is led by managing partner Dennis Podlesak and sponsored at Canaan by general partner Brent Ahrens, and operates from San Francisco, California, with an associated holding entity registered in Connecticut at Canaan's Westport office. Rather than operating as a product company, Axcelius assembles management teams and capital around licensed therapeutic assets and spins them out as standalone biopharma companies; Transposon Therapeutics, developing therapies for ALS and Alzheimer's disease, is its best-documented creation. As of this enrichment pass the vehicle remains in stealth mode with no public developer surface -- no product website beyond a holding page, no documentation, developer portal, SDKs, GitHub organization, or API of any kind.

providers.name: bayomics
providers.description: Bayomics (贝普奥生物) is a Shenzhen-based biotechnology company specializing in spatial proteomics and trace (micro) proteomics solutions for pharmaceutical research and drug development. Its product lines include the SISPROT protein sample-preparation kits built on proprietary Spintip centrifuge-pipette technology that process nanogram-level samples in roughly two hours, VistaProX spatial visualization proteomics combining immunofluorescence staining with high-depth mass-spectrometry detection on a single slice, and high-throughput automation systems capable of processing up to 400 proteomics samples per day. Bayomics operates as a B2B reagent supplier and research-services provider and does not currently publish any public developer API, SDKs, or programmatic developer resources. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: BeiGene
providers.description: BeiGene (rebranded as BeOne Medicines in 2025) is a global oncology biopharmaceutical company founded in 2010, developing and commercializing cancer therapies worldwide. Its portfolio spans blood cancers and solid tumors, led by BRUKINSA (zanubrutinib), a BTK inhibitor, alongside programs in protein degradation (CDACs) and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). The company is listed on NASDAQ (BGNE), HKEX, and the Shanghai STAR Market, with a global footprint across 30+ countries (beonemedicines.com). Surfaced as a portfolio company of Hillhouse; no public developer portal, API, or SDK program is currently published.

providers.name: Bionaut Labs
providers.description: Bionaut Labs is a clinical-stage medical robotics company headquartered in Los Angeles, California, developing "Bionauts" — remote-controlled, magnetically steered microscale robots roughly the size of a grain of rice that travel through tissue to deliver drugs, biologics and nucleic acids directly to targets deep in the brain and central nervous system. Founded in 2016 by CEO Michael Shpigelmacher, the company is pursuing treatments for malignant glioma, Dandy-Walker syndrome, Parkinson's disease and Huntington's disease, and has raised more than $80 million from investors including Khosla Ventures. Its product is a therapeutic device and navigation platform regulated as a medical device, not software sold to developers: Bionaut Labs operates no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: BioOrbit
providers.description: BioOrbit is a London-based in-space manufacturing company, founded in 2023, that uses microgravity to crystallise protein-based biologic drugs at scale. Its autonomous BOX hardware — a compact, microwave-sized manufacturing unit designed to operate in low-Earth orbit — grows highly ordered crystalline forms of therapeutic proteins that reduce viscosity, enabling treatments normally given intravenously (including cancer therapies) to be reformulated as subcutaneous, self-injectable products. Co-founded by Dr Katie King and Dr Leonor Teles, BioOrbit raised the world's largest seed round for in-space manufacturing (~£9.8M / $13.2M) co-led by LocalGlobe and Breega with Seedcamp, Auxxo, Type One, 7percent and angels, and is supported by the UK Space Agency, ESA BIC and ESA BSGN. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Seedcamp portfolio company; it publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Bioyond Robotics
providers.description: Bioyond Robotics (奔曜科技) is a life-sciences intelligent-automation company founded in 2021 and headquartered in Shanghai's Zhangjiang Science City. It combines robotics, machine vision, and artificial intelligence to build autonomous laboratory solutions for scientific research, drug discovery, applied chemistry, synthetic biology, multiomics, and clinical diagnostics. Its product line spans the LabGenius robot platform (liquid-handling and transport robots), the LabMate automation platform (material/liquid handling, stackers, and intelligent scheduling), the LabMind laboratory software platform for integrating external instruments and modules, and the BIOYOND AutoSeq genetic-analysis system. Bioyond is backed by Qiming Venture Partners. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — this record captures its identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: BlackThorn Therapeutics *
providers.description: BlackThorn Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2015 and headquartered in South San Francisco, focused on discovering and developing targeted therapeutics for brain diseases and central nervous system (CNS) disorders such as major depressive disorder and schizophrenia, using a precision-medicine platform. It was backed by gv (Google Ventures) and later combined into Neumora Therapeutics, whose corporate site now resolves at neumoratx.com. This is a life-sciences company profile: it operates no public developer API, SDK, or agent surface, so API-oriented artifacts are not applicable beyond a domain-security probe of the corporate host.

providers.name: cansinotech
providers.description: CanSino Biologics (康希诺生物, cansinotech.com.cn / cansinotech.com) is a Tianjin-based Chinese biopharmaceutical company founded in 2009 and dual-listed on the Hong Kong and Shanghai (STAR) exchanges. It researches, manufactures, and commercializes human vaccines across five proprietary technology platforms, with a portfolio covering COVID-19, meningococcal, pneumococcal, tuberculosis, Ebola, and DTcP indications. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation; only its corporate web presence was found.

providers.name: Caraway Health *
providers.description: Caraway Health is a digital health company that provides virtual mental and physical healthcare designed for college and university students, delivered through a mobile app with support offered around the clock. The company partners with higher-education institutions and is backed by GV (Google Ventures). It operates as a direct-to-consumer / campus telehealth provider rather than an API platform; at the time of this enrichment pass no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification was found on its public web surface. Sector: life-sciences / digital health.

providers.name: Celltype
providers.description: CellType is an AI-driven drug discovery company building what it calls "The Biological World Model" — foundation models and autonomous agents that simulate human biology to predict drug responses in human systems before clinical trials, reducing reliance on traditional preclinical models such as mice and cell lines. Its core technology, Cell2Sentence (C2S), teaches large language models to understand cellular biology by converting single-cell gene expression data into a text-like format that models can interpret, and the company reports using it to discover and validate a novel cancer treatment signal targeting tumor immunogenicity. A Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company based in New York City, CellType works with large pharmaceutical partners and currently operates as a B2B research and drug-discovery platform rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Cerexa
providers.description: Cerexa was a privately held biopharmaceutical company founded in the mid-2000s (its cerexa.com domain was registered in March 2005) to develop anti-infective therapies for serious, drug-resistant bacterial infections in the hospital setting. Its lead program was ceftaroline fosamil, a fifth-generation cephalosporin antibiotic active against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), in-licensed from Takeda Pharmaceutical Company and carried forward by Forest Laboratories; the compound was approved by the FDA on October 29, 2010 and marketed as Teflaro in the United States and Zinforo in Europe. Cerexa was backed by venture investors including Canaan Partners, and its programs ultimately passed through Forest Laboratories into the Actavis/Allergan combination (Forest Laboratories was acquired by Actavis on July 1, 2014) and on to AbbVie. Cerexa no longer operates as an independent company and has no developer surface: it publishes no API, no SDKs, no GitHub organization and no documentation, and its historical cerexa.com domain is now registered and operated by AbbVie, 301-redirecting to AbbVie's Allergan page. This profile is retained as a historical company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Chimerix
providers.description: Chimerix, Inc. was a biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Durham, North Carolina, focused on developing medicines for serious and life-threatening diseases. It is best known for brincidofovir (TEMBEXA), an antiviral approved by the U.S. FDA in 2021 as a smallpox medical countermeasure, and for dordaviprone (ONC201), an investigational small-molecule therapy for H3 K27M-mutant diffuse glioma, a form of brain cancer. Chimerix was a publicly traded company (NASDAQ: CMRX) and was acquired by Jazz Pharmaceuticals in 2025, primarily for dordaviprone; the chimerix.com domain now redirects to jazzpharma.com. As a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company, Chimerix does not operate a public developer program or API surface — this profile tracks it as a company entity within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ChronicleBio
providers.description: ChronicleBio is a biotechnology company working at the intersection of human data and drug discovery, with the stated mission of translating human data into disease-defining medicines. It operates in the healthcare and life-sciences sector and was surfaced through the electric-capital portfolio. As of this profile, ChronicleBio publishes a corporate marketing website but no public developer surface: enrichment found no API documentation, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, MCP server, or changelog. Domain security was probed live (TLS 1.3, HSTS, SPF, and a DMARC quarantine policy present; DNSSEC and CAA absent).

providers.name: CivaTech Oncology
providers.description: CivaTech Oncology is a Durham, North Carolina medical device manufacturer that develops polymer-encapsulated low dose rate (LDR) brachytherapy radiation sources for the treatment of solid tumors. Its FDA-cleared product line includes CivaSheet, a flexible, bioabsorbable, unidirectional planar source that can be custom-sized in the operating room and shields healthy tissue; CivaString, a polymer-encapsulated brachytherapy seed used for prostate and other localized cancers; and CivaDerm for dermatological applications. The company markets to radiation oncologists and surgical teams across pancreatic, sarcoma, colorectal, gynecologic, head and neck, lung and prostate indications, and its research has been supported by NIH/NCI and SBIR programs. It publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: cmlabs
providers.description: CMLabs (千麦医疗 / Qianmai Medical) is an independent third-party clinical laboratory group headquartered in China. It operates a network of medical testing laboratories that provide clinical laboratory diagnostics, pathology diagnosis, routine and specialty blood testing, clinical trial and research testing, and laboratory information system (LIS) services to hospitals, clinics, and other medical institutions. The company is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Comanche Biopharma
providers.description: Comanche Biopharma is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Concord, Massachusetts, developing investigational siRNA (small interfering RNA) medicines for maternal health. Its lead candidate, CBP-4888, is a subcutaneously administered siRNA therapy targeting sFlt1-mediated preterm preeclampsia, a leading and potentially life-threatening complication of pregnancy. The company's mission is to develop and make globally available the first therapy targeting a root cause of preeclampsia. In April 2025, CBP-4888 received Orphan Drug Designation from the European Medicines Agency. Comanche Biopharma is a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures). As a therapeutics company it publishes a corporate and scientific web presence rather than a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Corsair Pharma
providers.description: Corsair Pharma, Inc. is a privately held clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing proprietary prodrugs of treprostinil for the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Its lead program, the TRX-248 transdermal system, is an investigational once-daily patch that delivers an inactive treprostinil prodrug across the skin for conversion to active drug in the liver, aiming to combine the efficacy and titration profile of parenteral prostacyclin therapy with non-invasive once-daily dosing. The company completed its preclinical program, announced positive Phase 1 results for TRX-248 in June 2026, closed a $23M Series B led by New Rhein Healthcare Investors, and has entered a strategic collaboration with United Therapeutics to advance novel treprostinil prodrugs. Corsair Pharma is a drug developer, not a software vendor: its public web presence is a five-page marketing and investor-news site with no developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: CSR Biotech
providers.description: CSR Biotech (超视计 / Chaoshiji) is a Chinese life-sciences instrumentation company that develops super-resolution optical microscopy systems for advanced biological research. Its product line includes the HIS-SIM and MI-SIM structured-illumination microscopes and the SIM-Ultimate platform, delivering live-cell imaging down to roughly 60nm resolution across many imaging modes. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As a scientific-instruments maker, CSR Biotech publishes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: CTRL Therapeutics
providers.description: CTRL Therapeutics (cTRL Tx) is a Chicago-based preclinical biotechnology company developing next-generation cell therapies for solid tumors. The company harnesses circulating tumor-reactive lymphocytes (cTRLs) - a rare, potent T cell population found in the blood and naturally equipped to fight cancer - to engineer polyclonal cell therapies that avoid invasive tumor-tissue surgery. From a single blood draw, CTRL's proprietary IsoQore cell-sorting platform isolates millions of migratory, tumor-reactive cTRLs via novel markers, aiming to simplify the discovery, manufacturing and administration of solid-tumor cell therapy. CTRL launched in 2023 with a $10M seed financing led by General Catalyst, with participation from Intermountain Health and FACIT. This profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company operates a corporate website and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: D2G Oncology
providers.description: D2G Oncology is a precision-oncology company based in Mountain View, California, reported to have been founded in 2018 by Ian Winters. Public company descriptions characterize its work as applying quantitative and multiplexed functional cancer genomics to relate drugs to genotypes in order to advance precision cancer therapeutics. The company operates INSITE, a login-gated internal research portal at www.d2g-insite.com supporting preclinical study management and result exploration. D2G Oncology publishes no public developer API program, no developer portal, no API documentation, and no client SDKs, and third-party company trackers list the company as inactive as of 2026. It was surfaced through the Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio and is retained here as an identity-only profile.

providers.name: Danaher
providers.description: Danaher Corporation is a global life sciences and diagnostics conglomerate whose operating companies include Beckman Coulter, Leica Microsystems, Cepheid, SCIEX, IDT, Cytiva, Abcam, Aldevron, Beckman Coulter Diagnostics, Radiometer, and others. Danaher itself does not publish a corporate-level developer API; product and service APIs are provided by individual operating companies under the Danaher portfolio.

providers.name: Data Driven Bioscience
providers.description: Data Driven Bioscience (now operating as Duoseq, a ddb.bio service) is a cancer genomics testing company that performs comprehensive molecular profiling of both DNA and RNA from a single sample in an on-site workflow, delivering results from sample to report in roughly two days. Its platform detects mutations, expression levels, gene fusions, and clonotype information, and integrates directly with Epic and other leading EHR systems so results flow into the patient chart. The company is a portfolio company of initialized-capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; as of this pass it publishes a marketing/clinical website but no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Decibel Therapeutics *
providers.description: Decibel Therapeutics was a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on gene therapies for hearing loss and balance disorders. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV (Google Ventures) and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain, decibeltx.com, 301-redirects to regeneron.com, consistent with the company having been acquired/absorbed by Regeneron; Decibel maintains no independent public developer portal, API, documentation, or other developer surface. This profile is retained as a network lead and carries only infrastructure-level (domain security) probe data.

providers.name: Deep 6 AI
providers.description: Deep 6 AI was a clinical-trial acceleration company that used artificial intelligence and natural language processing to mine structured and unstructured clinical data in electronic health records, matching eligible patients to clinical trials in minutes rather than months. The Techstars-backed precision-research platform was acquired by Tempus AI in early 2024, after which its standalone deep6.ai web presence was retired (the domain no longer serves a site, though its email/DNS records remain active). No public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or package registry entries could be found for Deep 6 AI during enrichment.

providers.name: Elixiron Immunotherapeutics
providers.description: Elixiron Immunotherapeutics (Cayman) Limited is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2017, with offices in Taipei, Taiwan and Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing precision immunotherapies for neuroinflammation, autoimmune disease and cancer. Its clinical pipeline is led by enrupatinib (EI-1071), a small-molecule CSF-1R inhibitor in development for Alzheimer's disease and other neurodegenerative indications, and EI-001, a fully human anti-interferon-gamma monoclonal antibody in Phase 2 for vitiligo, alongside preclinical EI-012 (anti-CD36) and EI-220 (mRNA) oncology programs. The company publishes a corporate and investor-relations website only: there is no developer portal, public API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification of any kind on its own hosts.

providers.name: Epiodyne
providers.description: Epiodyne is a San Francisco-based pharmaceutical company using structure-based drug discovery to develop small-molecule opioid medicines precisely calibrated for minimal side effects and minimal addiction potential. Its pipeline targets pain management and opioid use disorder (OUD), engineering compounds with specifically tuned receptor functions to address the opioid crisis. The company is a venture-backed biotech portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or technology platform.

providers.name: EQRx
providers.description: EQRx was a biopharmaceutical company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2020 by Alexis Borisy with a mission to develop and deliver innovative, patent-protected medicines at radically lower prices. The company went public in 2021 through a SPAC merger with CM Life Sciences III and built an oncology and immunology pipeline anchored by in-licensed candidates such as aumolertinib and sugemalimab. In 2023 EQRx wound down its drug-development programs and was acquired by Revolution Medicines in an all-stock transaction. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead (backed by a16z and GV); it never operated a public developer platform or API, and its web presence is no longer live.

providers.name: Eureka Therapeutics
providers.description: Eureka Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Emeryville, California, developing T-cell therapies for solid tumors and hematologic malignancies. The company was founded by Dr. Cheng Liu and is built on two proprietary platforms: E-ALPHA, a high-throughput human antibody discovery engine used to find binders against cancer-specific targets, and ARTEMIS, an engineered T-cell receptor platform (AbTCR) designed to deliver CAR-T-level potency with a reduced cytokine-release profile. Its clinical programs include ET140203 (ARYA-1 in adults, ARYA-2 in pediatrics) and ECT204 (ARYA-3) in advanced liver cancer, alongside a GPC2 ARTEMIS T-cell program for neuroblastoma licensed from the National Cancer Institute. Eureka publishes a corporate website, pipeline and technology overviews, a press-release archive with an RSS feed, and patient-facing trial information; as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Evelo Biosciences *
providers.description: Evelo Biosciences was a Flagship Pioneering-founded, GV-backed microbiome biotechnology company in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing orally delivered investigational medicines acting on the small intestinal axis. Following clinical failures of its lead candidates EDP1815 and EDP2939, the company announced dissolution in November 2023 and has been wound down. It is retained in the API Evangelist network as a dissolved life-sciences portfolio record: the evelobio.com domain now serves only a parked catch-all error page and the company publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API surface of any kind.

providers.name: Everyone Medicines
providers.description: Everyone Medicines is a therapeutics company listed in the Khosla Ventures portfolio under the Therapeutics category, where it is described as "individualized precision therapeutics." The company has no public developer or API surface as of July 2026. Its original web address, everyonemedicines.com, now issues a 301 redirect to www.eomeds.com, a domain registered through GoDaddy on 2024-05-11 that currently resolves to no DNS A record, so the site is dark and no page, documentation, or .well-known document can be retrieved. Probes of the package registries (npm, PyPI), GitHub organizations (everyonemedicines, eomeds), and the .well-known discovery surface all returned nothing. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed life-sciences lead; it carries probed domain-security data only and should be re-run once the company publishes a live site.

providers.name: Evonetix
providers.description: Evonetix is a Cambridge, UK deep-technology company developing a benchtop DNA synthesis platform built on semiconductor technology. Its core innovation is a silicon chip carrying thousands of independently thermally-controlled reaction sites, allowing many DNA strands to be synthesised in parallel with per-site temperature control, in-process error detection and correction, and assembly of high-fidelity genes at the desktop. The company's goal is to give synthetic biology, life-science, and drug-discovery researchers accurate, on-demand access to synthetic DNA without relying on centralised outsourced gene foundries. Evonetix was surfaced as a portfolio company of the deep-tech venture firm DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK, and its primary web domain (evonetix.com) resolves to a suspended-account placeholder page.

providers.name: Excision
providers.description: Excision BioTherapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing CRISPR-based in vivo gene-editing therapies aimed at curing serious viral infectious diseases. Its programs apply multiplexed CRISPR editing delivered via AAV vectors to excise viral DNA from the host genome, led by EBT-101, an investigational one-time therapy for HIV. Excision is a therapeutics company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio company record rather than an API producer.

providers.name: Excision BioTherapeutics
providers.description: Excision BioTherapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing CRISPR-based gene-editing therapies intended to functionally cure serious viral infectious diseases. Its programs use multiplexed CRISPR/Cas approaches delivered via adeno-associated virus (AAV) to excise latent viral DNA from infected cells, with a lead candidate (EBT-101) targeting HIV and additional research directed at herpesviruses and hepatitis B. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As a therapeutics company it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile therefore carries company identity and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Exo Therapeutics
providers.description: Exo Therapeutics is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of crv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Forty Seven *
providers.description: Forty Seven, Inc. was an immuno-oncology biotechnology company founded in 2015 to commercialize CD47 immune-evasion research licensed from Stanford University (Irv Weissman and colleagues). Its lead program was magrolimab, a monoclonal antibody targeting CD47 — the "do not eat me" signal tumor cells use to evade macrophage-mediated killing — studied in myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Backed by GV, the company was acquired by Gilead Sciences in 2020 for roughly $4.9 billion; the fortyseveninc.com domain now redirects to gilead.com. As a clinical-stage therapeutics company it exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Genesis Therapeutics
providers.description: Genesis Therapeutics (Genesis Molecular AI) is an AI-focused biotechnology company building GEMS (Genesis Exploration of Molecular Space), a generative and predictive AI operating system for small-molecule drug discovery. GEMS combines structure-based deep learning, language and diffusion models, and physics-based simulation (molecular dynamics and quantum chemistry) to generate and optimize molecules for complex targets, accelerating hit identification through lead optimization and candidate selection. In 2025 the company introduced Pearl, a next-generation foundation model for drug discovery. Headquartered in Burlingame, California with a laboratory in San Diego, Genesis has raised over $300M and partners with Eli Lilly, Gilead, Genentech, and Incyte while advancing its own therapeutic pipeline. It is not a public API provider: GEMS is a proprietary internal platform with no published developer portal, documentation, or API.

providers.name: Genomics Medicine Ireland
providers.description: Genomics Medicine Ireland (GMI) is a Dublin-based life-sciences company founded in 2015 to build a large-scale Irish genomic and clinical research programme, sequencing volunteer participant DNA and pairing it with longitudinal phenotypic data to study the genetic basis of common and rare diseases such as Alzheimer's, heart failure, inflammatory bowel disease and multiple sclerosis. GMI was absorbed into WuXi NextCODE and subsequently rebranded as Genuity Science (genuitysci.com), a precision-medicine business offering disease-enriched genomic cohorts, whole-genome and next-generation sequencing through a clinically accredited lab, and population-scale data-analysis services to pharmaceutical and biotech partners for target discovery and biomarker identification. As a genomics research and data-services organization it exposes no public developer API, portal, SDKs or OpenAPI; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/portfolio lead and carries only the artifacts that can be honestly derived or probed for it.

providers.name: Gritstone Oncology
providers.description: Gritstone Oncology is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: life-sciences. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Helix Nano
providers.description: Helix Nano (HelixNano) is a Boston-based biotechnology company developing new ways to manipulate messenger RNA (mRNA) — the molecule that carries instructions from genes to the cell's protein-making machinery. Backed by DCVC since 2017, the company has developed techniques to improve the effectiveness and specificity of mRNA vaccines, including a next-generation COVID-19 vaccine engineered to resist viral mutation. HelixNano is now pursuing a broader vision of self-designing, adaptive therapeutics — drugs that could improve with every patient and, ideally, require only a single dose. The company operates out of 5 Channel Center Street in Boston, Massachusetts, and remains at an early, largely stealth stage with no public developer program or API surface at this time.

providers.name: IconOVir Bio
providers.description: IconOVir Bio is a New York City-based, clinical-stage life sciences company whose stated mission is to cure cancer and restore life to patients. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) as a portfolio company, IconOVir Bio operates in the oncology and cancer immunotherapy space, developing therapeutics aimed at treating patients across a range of cancers. The company maintains a corporate presence at 689 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan and presents a single-page corporate website with no public developer program, API, SDKs, or technical documentation. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a life-sciences portfolio lead; the enrichment pass confirmed there is no public API or developer surface to catalog beyond basic web-domain security posture.

providers.name: Immunis
providers.description: Immunis, Inc. is a private, clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Irvine, California, developing immunomodulatory secretome biologics — the mixture of proteins and factors secreted by stem cells, rather than the cells themselves — as a treatment for age- and disease-related immune decline. Its lead candidate, IMM01-STEM, is under study in the STEM-MYO Phase 1/2a trial for muscle atrophy and sarcopenia, alongside a STEM-META Phase 2 program and a STEM-K9 veterinary program. Immunis is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it publishes no developer portal, API, SDK, webhook surface, or machine-readable API contract of any kind. Its entire public surface is a WordPress marketing and clinical-trial-recruitment site whose only machine-readable endpoint is the default WordPress REST API at /wp-json/, which serves the CMS of that site and is not an Immunis API product.

providers.name: Immunos Therapeutics
providers.description: Immunos Therapeutics is a privately held biotechnology company focused on harnessing the immune system to treat cancer and inflammatory diseases. The company develops immuno-oncology and immunomodulatory therapeutic candidates, advancing a preclinical and clinical pipeline supported by scientific and clinical advisory boards. Immunos Therapeutics is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As a therapeutics/drug-development company it operates in the life sciences rather than as a software API provider, and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer documentation at this time. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company and portfolio discovery.

providers.name: Innovent
providers.description: Innovent Biologics (信达生物制药) is a biopharmaceutical company founded in 2011 and headquartered in the Suzhou Industrial Park, China, that discovers, develops, manufactures, and commercializes high-quality biologic medicines for the treatment of oncology, autoimmune, cardiovascular and metabolic, and ophthalmology diseases. Its portfolio includes the PD-1 inhibitor Tyvyt (sintilimab), developed in partnership with Eli Lilly, alongside a broad pipeline of monoclonal antibodies and other biologics. Innovent is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (01801.HK) and was surfaced through the Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China) portfolio. Innovent is a therapeutics company and does not publish a public developer API surface; this profile captures its corporate and domain-security identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Instylla
providers.description: Instylla, Inc. is a privately held medical device company headquartered in Bedford, Massachusetts, founded in 2017 by Incept LLC to develop next-generation resorbable liquid embolic agents for interventional radiology, with initial clinical applications in interventional oncology and peripheral hemostasis. Its flagship product, the Embrace Hydrogel Embolic System, received U.S. FDA premarket approval (PMA) in August 2025 for the embolization of hypervascular tumors in peripheral arteries of 5 mm or less, and began commercial use in January 2026; the company also markets the FDA-cleared Tembo Embolic System. Embrace is delivered as two injectable polyethylene-glycol precursors that crosslink in the vessel lumen into a soft hydrogel and then resorb by hydrolysis over roughly eleven months. Instylla is a device manufacturer rather than a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: InterVenn
providers.description: InterVenn Biosciences is a digital-biology company applying artificial intelligence and mass spectrometry to glycoproteomics, the large-scale study of glycosylated proteins, to discover novel biomarkers for precision medicine. Its proprietary platform integrates liquid chromatography and tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS) with AI-driven analysis (including the OpenPIP software) to identify and quantify glycopeptides and glycan structures across complex diseases such as cancer. Surfaced as a portfolio company of amplify-partners and softbank-vision-fund and added to the API Evangelist network. InterVenn publishes no public developer API, portal, or specifications as of this enrichment pass; this profile carries company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Invetx *
providers.description: Invetx was a Boston-based veterinary biotechnology company developing protein-based therapeutics — species-specific, half-life-extended monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) — for chronic conditions in companion animals (dogs and cats). Its integrated platform spanned antibody discovery, optimization, Fc-variant half-life extension, development and manufacturing, with lead program IVX-01.
