Backed by GV, F-Prime Capital, Novo Holdings, Eight Roads, Anterra Capital, Casdin Capital and Tekla, Invetx was acquired by Dechra Pharmaceuticals in July 2024 for up to $520M. It exposes no public API, developer, or documentation surface, and its standalone website (invetx.com) has been decommissioned since the acquisition; this profile is retained as a network lead / portfolio record.

providers.name: Iolyx Therapeutics
providers.description: Iolyx Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Burlingame, California, working at what it calls the intersection of immunology and ophthalmology — "immuno-ophthalmology". The company develops immunomodulatory therapeutics that target ocular inflammation at its source, using what it describes as innovative pathways and tailored formulations for precise delivery to the relevant ocular tissues, positioned as an alternative to conventional steroids and broad immunosuppressants. Its lead asset, ILYX-002, is in trials for autoimmune-associated dry eye disease; the company announced Phase 2 results in May 2025 and, in December 2025, a strategic agreement with Laboratoires Théa to develop and commercialize ILYX-002 alongside Series B funding for its retinal pipeline. The stated pipeline spans front-of-eye indications (dry eye, ocular allergy, rosacea, uveitis) and back-of-eye indications (age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy, posterior uveitis). Iolyx is a drug developer rather than a software vendor: it operates a six-page WordPress marketing site at iolyx.com and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: jfkbio
providers.description: jfkbio (今复康生物科技 / JFK Bio) is a biotechnology and life-sciences company in China, surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its public presence at jfkbio.com is a JavaScript single-page marketing site; no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, or other machine-readable API surface was found during enrichment, so most API artifact types are not applicable to this provider. This profile records what is genuinely observable today (identity and live domain-security posture) and remains a lead pending any future developer or API surface.

providers.name: Kinaset Therapeutics
providers.description: Kinaset Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Medfield, Massachusetts, founded in 2020 by Robert Clarke (CEO), Roger Heerman (COO) and Frazer Morgan (CDO) to develop novel inhaled therapeutics for severe respiratory disease. Its lead candidate, frevecitinib (KN-002), is a dry-powder inhaled pan-JAK inhibitor — potent and balanced across JAK1, JAK2, JAK3 and TYK2 — designed as a non-invasive anti-inflammatory add-on to standard of care for all severe asthma patients regardless of the underlying cause of inflammation, and explored in COPD. The company completed a Phase 1/1b program (NCT05006521), received FDA IND clearance, and in July 2026 dosed the first patient in the Phase 2b PANAIRAMA trial (NCT07532265) after closing a $103M oversubscribed Series B in January 2026 led by RA Capital Management and Forge Life Science Partners, with EQT Life Sciences, Vivo Capital, Schroders Capital, Willett Advisors, Pictet Alternative Advisors, Sixty Degree Capital, Atlas Venture, 5AM Ventures and Gimv participating on roughly $143M raised to date. Kinaset is a drug developer, not a software company: its product is a clinical pipeline, and it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDKs, no webhooks and no machine-readable API contract. Its entire public surface is a 34-page Squarespace marketing and investor-news site whose robots.txt disallows every platform JSON view and blocks the major AI crawlers by user agent.

providers.name: Kronos Bio *
providers.description: Kronos Bio was a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in the life-sciences sector, backed by GV, working on cancer therapeutics. providers.name: Mozart Therapeutics
providers.description: Mozart Therapeutics, Inc. is a privately held, clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company in Seattle, Washington, founded in 2020 to develop disease-modifying therapies for autoimmune and inflammatory disease. Its pipeline comprises MTX-101, a KIR x CD8 bispecific antibody in Phase 1b study for type 1 diabetes, and MTX-201, a KIR x ICOS bispecific in preclinical development for inflammatory bowel disease. Stilla was acquired by Bio-Rad Laboratories (announced February 2025, ~$225M plus up to $50M in milestones, closed 2025); its web properties now redirect to Bio-Rad. The company operates laboratory hardware and consumables rather than a public developer platform — no OpenAPI, developer portal, SDKs, CLI, or MCP surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Stipple Bio
providers.description: Stipple Bio is a preclinical precision-oncology biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2022 by cancer-biology researchers Aaron Ring (Fred Hutch) and Aashish Manglik (UCSF). Its Pointillist Platform performs cellular profiling and tumor-specific epitope discovery to design antibody binders and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) that target tumor-specific cell-surface epitopes while avoiding on-target, off-tumor toxicity. Its lead asset, STP-100, is an ADC advancing toward early clinical studies. The company emerged from stealth in April 2026 with an oversubscribed $100M Series A co-led by RA Capital, a16z Bio+Health and Nextech Invest, with participation from Google Ventures (gv). As a therapeutics company, Stipple Bio publishes no public API, developer portal, or software developer surface.

providers.name: Stylus Medicine
providers.description: Stylus Medicine is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company developing in vivo genetic medicines built on engineered recombinases. Its platform aims to generate precise, durable CAR-T cells directly inside the body using cell-targeted lipid nanoparticle delivery to immune cells, with therapeutic programs spanning oncology, autoimmune disease, and genetic disorders. The company is a portfolio company of Khosla Ventures. It operates as a research-stage therapeutics company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Superluminal Medicines
providers.description: Superluminal Medicines is a drug discovery company that combines structure-based drug discovery with AI-powered computational methods and experimental validation to identify and develop small molecule therapeutics. Its pipeline targets G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) for cardiometabolic disease and obesity, including a collaboration with Eli Lilly worth up to $1.3 billion. Backed by Insight Partners. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface was found as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: SURGE Therapeutics
providers.description: SURGE Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing intraoperative cancer immunotherapy. Founded on research from Dr. Michael Goldberg's laboratory at Harvard Medical School, the company's SURGERx platform is an injectable, biodegradable hydrogel placed directly at the site of surgical tumor resection to provide extended, localized release of immunotherapy — addressing the surgery-induced inflammation that suppresses the immune system and allows residual disease to reawaken. Its lead program, SRG-514, completed Phase 1 dose escalation in breast cancer patients undergoing surgery and is being prepared for a registrational trial, with an additional IND cleared for a Phase 1/2a study in bladder cancer. SURGE has raised a $26M Series A and a $32M Series B. It is a therapeutics developer, not a software company, and publishes no developer program, API, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Syremis Therapeutics
providers.description: Syremis Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Tel Aviv, Israel and Boston, Massachusetts, developing best-in-class oral small-molecule medicines for serious mental health conditions. Its neuropsychiatric pipeline is rooted in clinically validated mechanisms including muscarinic M1/M4 agonism and next-generation NMDA antagonism; lead program ST-905 is a dual M1/M4 agonist in Phase 1 for schizophrenia, with ST-901 also spun out from Clexio Biosciences. The company launched publicly in December 2025 with a $165M Series A co-led by Dexcel Pharma and Third Rock Ventures, with participation from Bain Capital Life Sciences, GV (Google Ventures), QVT, and Pictet. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of GV. This company publishes no public API, developer, or event surface at this time.

providers.name: Taysha Gene Therapies *
providers.description: Taysha Gene Therapies is a clinical-stage biotechnology company (Dallas, TX with a laboratory in Morrisville, NC) developing AAV-based gene therapies for rare monogenic diseases of the central nervous system. Its lead program, TSHA-102, targets Rett syndrome and has completed dosing in the REVEAL pivotal trial. The company operates as a therapeutics developer and publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or technical integration surface; it was surfaced as a GV portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: TenSixteen Bio
providers.description: TenSixteen Bio is a San Francisco-based clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering the study of somatic mosaicism and clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) to discover and develop novel therapeutics for age-related diseases including cancer and cardiovascular disease. Founded by CEO Mark Chao and launched in 2022 with a $40M Series A from Foresite Capital and GV (formerly Google Ventures), the company combines human genetics, functional genomics and next-generation-sequencing (NGS) based assays to identify CHIP-linked mutations and translate them into companion diagnostics and precision-medicine treatments. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; as a therapeutics and diagnostics company it publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: TenSixty Bio
providers.description: TenSixty Bio is an oncology-focused biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, working to revolutionize the treatment of cancer. The company combines biology, machine learning, and high-throughput technologies to build an atlas of antibody targets on the surface of cancer cells, discover novel cancer targets, and develop improved therapeutics from bench to bedside. TenSixty Bio is a privately held research-stage company backed by General Catalyst and Wing Venture Capital, and it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced through the API Evangelist venture-capital portfolio pipeline and enriched with verified public company identity.

providers.name: TRIANA Biomedicines
providers.description: TRIANA Biomedicines is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners, lightspeed-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: biotech. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: tripod-glp
providers.description: tripod-glp resolves to TriApex Laboratories, a next-generation pharmaceutical and biomedical contract research organization (CRO) headquartered in Nanjing, China with facilities in Shanghai, Kunming, Wenchang and Pennsylvania. TriApex provides integrated nonclinical services (safety assessment, efficacy, DMPK and research models) and clinical trial services across phases I-III, with disease expertise spanning cardiometabolic, CNS, ophthalmology, autoimmune and oncology. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network, it publishes a corporate website (www.tri-apex.com) but no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Trisk Bio
providers.description: Trisk Bio is a preclinical AAV (adeno-associated virus) manufacturing partner / CDMO that develops bespoke, scalable processes for AAV gene therapies to enable affordable preclinical manufacturing. It supplies research-grade and non-human primate (NHP) study-grade vectors across capsid serotypes and transgenes, offering custom process development, high-throughput optimisation of a single transgene against multiple capsids, and purification and supply of partials as reference material. Backed by Matrix Partners, Trisk Bio is a healthtech / biomanufacturing company; at the time of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing website but no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: TScan Therapeutics
providers.description: TScan Therapeutics (Nasdaq: TCRX) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company based in Waltham, Massachusetts developing T-cell receptor engineered T-cell (TCR-T) therapies for the treatment of patients with cancer. The company uses a high-throughput, genome-wide target-discovery platform to identify the TCRs and antigen targets that drive T-cell recognition of tumors, building a multiplexed library of TCR-T candidates (ImmunoBank) for both hematologic malignancies and solid tumors. Lead programs TSC-100 and TSC-101 target minor histocompatibility antigens to prevent disease relapse after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant. As a therapeutics company it exposes no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and GV.

providers.name: Verge Labs
providers.description: Verge Labs (formerly Verge Genomics) is a frontier AI company applying machine learning to human biology, building an AI system designed to reason about neurological disease at the patient level. Its stated goal is a "virtual biopsy of the brain" — a reconstructed picture of what is happening inside a patient's brain generated from a routine blood draw. The company built proprietary genomic datasets from human brain tissue for neurodegenerative diseases such as ALS and Parkinson's, and after an early ALS clinical program refocused on AI methods for matching brain therapeutics to the patients most likely to benefit. Verge is a research-stage biotech/AI company backed by Threshold Ventures and other venture investors; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal.

providers.name: Verve Therapeutics
providers.description: Verve Therapeutics is a Boston-based clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a pipeline of in vivo gene editing medicines designed to treat cardiovascular disease with a single, one-time treatment. Its programs use base editing and CRISPR technology to durably switch off disease-driving genes, led by VERVE-102 (targeting PCSK9 to lower LDL cholesterol), alongside VERVE-201 (ANGPTL3) and VERVE-301 (LPA). Verve was acquired by Eli Lilly in July 2025 in a deal worth up to $1.3 billion. As a therapeutics/research company it publishes no public developer API; this profile is maintained as a company identity record in the API Evangelist network. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of GV.

providers.name: Vicinitas Therapeutics
providers.description: Vicinitas Therapeutics is a biotechnology company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. It operates in the therapeutics and drug-discovery space (vicinitastx.com) and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface. This profile records what is verifiable about the company and remains a lead awaiting any future API footprint.

providers.name: Vir Biotechnology
providers.description: Vir Biotechnology is a clinical-stage immunology company that engineers antibodies into medicines targeting serious infectious diseases and cancer. Its programs span chronic hepatitis delta, hepatitis B, oncology, and prior work on COVID-19 and Ebola, built on a next-generation antibody platform and the licensed PRO-XTEN protease-releasable masking technology. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network. This is a corporate/investor-facing life-sciences company; enrichment probes found no public developer, API, or partner-integration surface.

providers.name: Viridos
providers.description: Viridos, founded in 2005 as Synthetic Genomics, Inc. by J. Craig Venter and Hamilton Smith and renamed Viridos in September 2021, was a La Jolla, California synthetic-biology company that engineered microalgae genomes to produce low-carbon-intensity biofuels, running its algal biofuel program as a long-term research partnership with ExxonMobil. The company never published an API, a developer portal, or any machine-readable contract; its only public developer surface was a GitHub organization holding two first-party open-source projects - the AGPL-licensed sgidspace deep-learning protein annotation library and a sensor calibration app - alongside seven forks of third-party tools. Viridos filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the District of Delaware on 2025-04-14, sold substantially all of its algae biofuel technology to Breakthrough Energy Ventures II, L.P., and the case was dismissed on 2025-11-26. Its website has served no content since roughly October 2025.

providers.name: Visterra
providers.description: Visterra is a Waltham, Massachusetts biologics research company developing antibody-based therapeutics for patients with immune-mediated and other difficult-to-treat diseases. It combines computational design, artificial intelligence, and experimental research with agile preclinical development and manufacturing. Visterra publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company tracking and enrichment.

providers.name: Vitara Biomedical
providers.description: Vitara Biomedical is a medical technology company developing EXTEND, a fluid-filled extra-uterine environment designed to protect the fragile lungs and vital organs of extremely premature newborns born before 24 weeks of gestation, delaying the stress of early air exposure for up to 28 days while their lungs and other organs continue to develop. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV in the life-sciences sector. The company is pre-market (no FDA clearance) and does not currently publish any public API, SDK, developer portal, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Waltz Health
providers.description: Waltz Health is a Chicago-based digital health company founded in 2021 by Mark Thierer (former CEO of OptumRx and Catamaran) and Jonathon Thierer, building AI-driven prescription drug pricing marketplaces that help consumers, payers, pharmacy benefit managers, pharmacies, and self-insured employers make better-informed, lower-cost decisions on prescription care. Its Marketplace Search product is a multi-card search engine that compares medication prices across every major discount and savings program, and Waltz Connect is an end-to-end solution that lowers the cost of specialty medications through a network of national and regional specialty pharmacies that compete on price and clinical outcomes. The company raised a $35M Series A led by GV and, in August 2025, merged with EVERSANA to form a combined pharmaceutical commercialization and drug-access platform, with Mark Thierer appointed CEO of EVERSANA. Waltz Health has no public developer API program; this profile captures company identity and live domain-security posture.

providers.name: Xilis
providers.description: Xilis is a life-sciences / precision-oncology company developing patient-derived MicroOrganoSphere (MOS) technology to model a patient's tumor outside the body for functional drug testing and drug discovery. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network. Enrichment probes found a marketing website only (SiteGround-hosted, bot-protection returns HTTP 403) with no public developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, or API surface of any kind.

providers.name: Dvlp Medicines
providers.description: DVLP Medicines is a drug-development software company building an end-to-end, configurable platform that moves molecules from discovery to commercialization with speed. The platform pairs a single data repository for pharmaceutical assets with specialized AI agents for pharma operations, document automation, knowledge synthesis, and decision support for portfolio management. It is positioned as a software co-pilot for drug development and a marketplace connecting project leaders with investors and outsourced R&D and manufacturing vendors, targeting underserved therapeutic markets such as new antibiotics for antimicrobial resistance and rare-disease therapies. DVLP Medicines is a portfolio company of DCVC (Computational Bio & Chem), first funded in 2022. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; the company publishes a marketing site but no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Eli Lilly
providers.description: Eli Lilly and Company is a Fortune 500 global pharmaceutical company that discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells human pharmaceutical products in therapeutic areas including diabetes, oncology, immunology, and neuroscience. Eli Lilly does not currently publish a public developer API portal; the company exposes selected machine learning models through its Lilly TuneLab platform to partner biotechs but does not offer general purpose, self-serve APIs.

providers.name: Revvity
providers.description: Revvity is a life sciences and diagnostics company providing instruments, software, reagents, and services to support drug discovery, development, diagnostics, and applied research. Formed from the former life sciences and diagnostics businesses of PerkinElmer, Revvity serves pharmaceutical, biotech, clinical, academic, and applied markets with offerings spanning reproductive health screening, omics, imaging, and laboratory automation.

providers.name: AllStripes
providers.description: AllStripes was a San Francisco healthcare technology company, founded in 2017 as RDMD by Nancy Yu and Onno Faber, that built a research platform dedicated to rare disease. It retrieved, digitized and de-identified patients' medical records into regulatory-ready real-world evidence for biopharma drug development, and paired that with a patient application through which families affected by conditions such as Batten disease, Hunter syndrome and sickle cell anemia could participate in treatment research from home. The company raised roughly $74M in venture funding, including a $50M Series B in August 2021 led by Lux Capital with JAZZ Venture Partners, Spark Capital, Medidata, McKesson Ventures and Maveron. PicnicHealth acquired AllStripes on October 23, 2023 and folded the platform into its own; the AllStripes brand has since been retired, and allstripes.com and app.allstripes.com now issue blanket 301 redirects to picnichealth.com. AllStripes never published a public developer portal, REST/OpenAPI contract, SDK, or webhook surface, and no such surface survives the acquisition.

providers.name: Arresto Biosciences
providers.description: Arresto Biosciences, Inc. was a privately-held, development-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Palo Alto, California, focused on medicines to treat fibrotic diseases and cancer by targeting enzymes involved in the synthesis of the extracellular matrix. Its lead product was AB0024, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting the human lysyl oxidase-like-2 (LOXL2) protein, then in Phase I studies for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and advanced solid tumors. Founded circa 2007 and backed by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, HealthCare Ventures, Northgate Capital, DAG Ventures and Abbott Biotech Ventures, Arresto was acquired by Gilead Sciences for $225 million; the deal was announced December 20, 2010 and had closed by February 2011. The company no longer operates as an independent entity, publishes no developer or API surface, and its former domain (arrestobio.com) no longer resolves.

providers.name: Arthrosi Therapeutics
providers.description: Arthrosi Therapeutics, Inc. is a late-stage clinical biotechnology company founded in 2018 and headquartered in San Diego, California, by a team of gout specialists who previously led first-generation urate-transporter development at Ardea Biosciences. Its lead candidate, pozdeutinurad (AR882), is a once-daily oral next-generation URAT1 inhibitor in two fully enrolled replicate global Phase 3 trials (REDUCE 1 and REDUCE 2) for progressive and tophaceous gout, backed by roughly $299M in venture financing including a $153M Series E led by Prime Eight Capital. Sobi (Swedish Orphan Biovitrum) completed its acquisition of Arthrosi on 9 February 2026. Arthrosi is a drug developer, not a software company: it operates a WordPress corporate site with company, leadership and news pages, and publishes no developer portal, public API, SDK, package or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Bambusa Therapeutics
providers.description: Bambusa Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in the Boston Seaport, founded in 2024 by Shanshan Xu and Helmut Jeggle to develop next-generation bispecific antibodies for immunological and inflammatory (I&I) diseases. Its antibody-engineering platform combines half-life extension with high-concentration subcutaneous delivery, and its pipeline spans dermatology, respiratory, gastroenterology and rheumatology — led by BBT-001 (IL-31 x IL-4Ralpha, in a Phase 1b/2a atopic dermatitis trial) and BBT-002 for COPD. The company raised a Series Seed in 2024, an approximately $90M Series A led by RA Capital Management in February 2025, and an oversubscribed Series A-2 in November 2025. It is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor, and publishes no public API, SDK or developer program.

providers.name: Entact Bio
providers.description: Entact Bio is a preclinical-stage biotechnology company based in Watertown, Massachusetts, developing a new class of small-molecule precision medicines called Enhancement-Targeting Chimeric (ENTAC) molecules. Where targeted protein degradation removes disease-causing proteins, Entact Bio works in the opposite direction: its ENTAC molecules recruit deubiquitinases (DUBs) to strip ubiquitin chains from beneficial proteins in order to extend their half-life, relocate them, or otherwise restore their function. The company's proprietary Encompass platform combines biological, chemical, and computational tools to identify disease targets amenable to protein enhancement across oncology, autoimmune disease, and rare genetic disorders. Entact Bio launched in December 2022 with an $81 million Series A co-led by Qiming Venture Partners USA and venBio Partners, with participation from Abingworth, Brandon Capital, and others. It is a therapeutics research organization and publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: Epic Sciences
providers.description: Epic Sciences is a San Diego, California clinical diagnostics company founded in 2008 that develops blood-based "liquid biopsy" tests for oncology. Its platform, licensed from the Peter Kuhn laboratory at Scripps Research, isolates and characterizes rare circulating tumor cells (CTCs) from whole blood using specialized assays and digital pathology algorithms, and is paired with circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) sequencing to inform treatment selection and track how a tumor evolves. Its lead product, DefineMBC, is a comprehensive blood biopsy for metastatic breast cancer whose 56-gene ctDNA panel received Medicare coverage in April 2023. The company also runs its platform as a service for pharmaceutical partners measuring outcomes in clinical trials, and in 2020 partnered with Predicine to combine CTC and ctDNA analysis in a single offering. Epic Sciences is privately held and has raised roughly $204M across seven rounds through a Series G in April 2023. It is a laboratory diagnostics provider, not a software vendor, and publishes no public API, developer program, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Faraday Pharmaceuticals
providers.description: Faraday Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was a Seattle, Washington clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company founded in 2014 as a spinout of Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, built on the elemental-reducing-agent research of Dr. Mark Roth. It developed therapies intended to prevent and treat cardiac and skeletal muscle loss after acute critical illness, led by FDY-5301 — a proprietary intravenous formulation of sodium iodide designed to neutralize reactive oxygen species and limit reperfusion injury in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention for anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The company raised roughly $120M from an investor group led by ARCH Venture Partners and Polaris Partners. Its Phase 3 trial read out in late 2025 and failed to meet its primary or secondary endpoints, and Faraday announced in February 2026 that it had ceased operations and was winding down the business. Faraday never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and its faradaypharma.com website is no longer served. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Korro Bio
providers.description: Korro Bio, Inc. (Nasdaq: KRRO) is a Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing a new class of genetic medicines based on programmable RNA editing. Its proprietary OPERA (Oligonucleotide Promoted Editing of RNA) platform pairs data-driven oligonucleotide design and machine-learning optimization with linker chemistry and tissue-directed delivery to recruit the body's own ADAR enzymes and make a precise, transient single-base edit to a native mRNA transcript — editing RNA rather than DNA so the change is tunable and reversible. The company was created and incubated by Atlas Venture with New Enterprise Associates in October 2019, raised a $91.5M Series A and a $116M Series B, and became public in 2023 through a merger with Frequency Therapeutics alongside a $117M private placement. Its pipeline targets liver and central nervous system indications and includes KRRO-110 (the REWRITE Phase 1/2a study in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency), KRRO-111 and KRRO-121, which holds EMA orphan drug designation for urea cycle disorders. Korro Bio sells therapeutics, not software: it operates no developer program, publishes no API, SDK or machine-readable specification, and maintains no public source-code organization.

providers.name: Latigo Bio
providers.description: Latigo Biotherapeutics, Inc. ("Latigo Bio") is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Thousand Oaks, California, developing novel non-opioid medicines for acute and chronic pain. Its lead candidates LTG-001 and LTG-321 are oral NaV1.8 sodium-channel inhibitors targeting pain at its peripheral source without the addiction risk of opioids; LTG-001 holds FDA Fast Track designation and reported positive Phase 2b results in post-abdominoplasty acute pain, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in July 2026. The company was founded on human-genetics-validated targets and uses in-house AI/ML and structure-based drug design to optimize potency and selectivity. It debuted in 2024 with a $135M Series A and closed a $150M Series B in March 2025, backed by Westlake Village BioPartners, 5AM Ventures, Foresite Capital and Corner Ventures. Latigo is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Mercy BioAnalytics
providers.description: Mercy BioAnalytics, Inc. is a Waltham, Massachusetts clinical-stage cancer diagnostics company, founded in 2018, developing extracellular-vesicle (EV) based liquid biopsy tests for the early detection of cancer. Its patented Mercy Halo platform uses biomarker co-localization — the simultaneous detection of multiple cancer-related biomarkers on the surface of individual tumor-derived extracellular vesicles — to read a small volume of serum or plasma with a simple PCR-based readout. The company's initial programs target ovarian cancer screening in asymptomatic post-menopausal women and lung cancer detection in average and high-risk individuals; the Mercy Halo Ovarian Cancer Screening Test received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation in May 2024. Mercy BioAnalytics raised a $41M Series A in April 2023 led by Novalis LifeSciences and a $59M Series B in September 2025. The product is a laboratory-developed blood test, not software: as of this profile the company publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Myra Vision
providers.description: Myra Vision, Inc. is a clinical-stage ophthalmic medical device company headquartered in Campbell, California, and a privately held portfolio company of the Shifamed LLC medical device incubator. It develops the Calibreye Titratable Glaucoma Therapy (TGT) Surgical System, an aqueous shunt for patients with moderate to severe glaucoma whose valve-controlled outflow channels use shape-memory nitinol and can be reversibly opened or closed in-office with a transcorneal laser, letting a clinician titrate intraocular pressure after implantation rather than committing to a fixed flow at the time of surgery. The company completed first-in-human use of the Calibreye System in 2023, received FDA conditional approval of its Investigational Device Exemption in August 2025, and enrolled the first patient in its US ADAPT clinical study in January 2026. As a medical device manufacturer its product is a physical implant and a surgical procedure, not software: Myra Vision publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification, and this profile captures its corporate identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Myrtelle
providers.description: Myrtelle, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Wakefield, Massachusetts, developing gene therapies for myelin-based disorders of the central nervous system. Its lead program, MYR-101 (rAAV-Olig001-ASPA), is a first-in-class oligotrophic recombinant adeno-associated virus gene therapy for Canavan disease, a rare and fatal childhood genetic brain disease caused by mutations in the ASPA gene. The program is licensed exclusively worldwide from Pfizer Inc., holds Orphan Drug, Fast Track and Rare Pediatric Disease designations in the US with similar designations in Europe, and has reported Phase 1/2 interim results in Nature Medicine. Myrtelle is a therapeutics developer, not a software company: it publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable API contract, and is profiled here for network completeness only.

providers.name: Presidio Medical
providers.description: Presidio Medical is a privately held, clinical-stage medical device company headquartered in South San Francisco, California, founded in 2017 by Kenneth Wu and led by CEO and Chairman Michael Onuscheck. It is developing an implantable Ultra Low Frequency (ULF) neuromodulation platform intended to treat diseases of undesired neural activity, with a first indication in chronic nociceptive low back pain. The therapy delivers ultra low frequency current through an epidural spinal cord stimulation (SCS) lead to reversibly inhibit pain-signaling neurons via sodium channel inactivation, positioned as a non-opioid alternative to conventional SCS. The company raised a $72M Series C in 2023 led by Deerfield Management with Invus Opportunities, Action Potential Venture Capital and ShangBay Capital, and received FDA IDE approval for the global pivotal FULFILL randomized controlled trial in the United States and Australia. Presidio Medical sells an implantable medical device, not software; it has never operated a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable API contract. As of 2026-08-05 its corporate WordPress site at presidiomedical.com is offline, returning a WP Engine "Site Not Configured" HTTP 404 on every path including the root.

providers.name: SCG Cell Therapy
providers.description: SCG Cell Therapy Pte. Ltd. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company headquartered in Singapore, with operations across Singapore, China and Germany, developing novel immunotherapies for infectious diseases and the cancers they cause. The company targets the most common cancer-causing infections — Helicobacter pylori, human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) — and is advancing a pipeline of TCR-engineered T cell therapies, antibodies and therapeutic vaccines built on its proprietary GianTCR platform. Lead programs include SCG101, a first-in-class autologous HBV-specific TCR-T therapy targeting hepatitis B surface antigen in HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma, and SCG142, a next-generation HPV E7-specific TCR-T therapy for HPV-associated solid tumors that received FDA IND clearance. SCG covers the full value chain from drug discovery and manufacturing through clinical development and commercialization. It is a therapeutics developer, not a software vendor, and publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Selkirk Pharma
providers.description: Selkirk Pharma, Inc. is a privately held U.S. contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) in Spokane, Washington, specializing in the aseptic fill/finish of sterile injectable drug products — vaccines, biologics and small molecules — for clinical and commercial supply. Founded in 2018, it operates a purpose-built aseptic campus at 9110 W Granite Avenue in the Pacific Northwest Technology Park, roughly half a mile from Spokane International Airport, running unidirectional personnel and material flow, single-use systems, SKAN isolator technology and Bausch+Strobel VarioSys dose-filling lines rated to about 3,600 vials per hour under EU GMP Annex 1. Services span aseptic filling, in-house analytical chemistry and microbiology, sterility testing, finished-product inspection, regulatory support and supply-chain services, plus a ClinFAST program that compresses fill/finish timelines for clinical-trial material. The build-out drew roughly $150M led by Spokane's Cowles Company with other Washington State investors, and Colleen Dixon was named chief executive in July 2024. Selkirk Pharma sells contract manufacturing capacity, not software: it operates no developer program, publishes no web API, SDK or machine-readable specification, and maintains no public source-code organization. (In this sector "API" ordinarily means active pharmaceutical ingredient; Selkirk fills and finishes drug product and publishes no web API.)

providers.name: Shoreline Biosciences
providers.description: Shoreline Biosciences was a San Diego, California clinical-stage biotechnology company developing off-the-shelf, allogeneic cell therapies from induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), principally iPSC-derived natural killer (iNK) cells and macrophages engineered for oncology indications. It raised roughly $140M, acquired Editas Medicine's iNK cell franchise and related gene-editing technologies in 2023, and signed collaborations with Kite Pharma (Gilead) and BeiGene with headline values above $4B. Therapeutics, not software, were the product: no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification was ever published. As of this profiling pass the company's own domain, shorelinebio.com, no longer serves a website — it answers HTTP 404 with a Squarespace "Website Expired" holding page — and the company is tracked here only as a secondary-market entity.

providers.name: Alexandria Real Estate Equities
providers.description: Alexandria Real Estate Equities is an urban office REIT and the leading owner, operator, and developer of life science, agtech, and technology campuses in AAA innovation cluster locations across the United States. The company partners with biotechnology, pharmaceutical, agtech, and technology firms to provide laboratory and office space, venture investments, and thought leadership. Alexandria Real Estate Equities does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal.

providers.name: Alphina Therapeutics
providers.description: Alphina Therapeutics is a New Haven, Connecticut precision-oncology biotechnology company founded by experts in DNA repair and metabolic lethality. It develops next-generation antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) that deliver potent NAMPT inhibitor payloads directly to tumors, designed to kill both dividing and non-dividing cancer cells, and pairs them with a proprietary companion diagnostic that identifies the patients most likely to respond. The company is venture-backed by Canaan Partners. It was surfaced as a portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation, so no API artifacts apply at this time.

providers.name: General Proximity
providers.description: General Proximity is a biotechnology company pioneering next-generation "proximity medicines" that control biological processes by inducing proximity between molecular targets. Its multi-target OMNITAC platform is used to discover and advance novel therapeutics, including an oncology collaboration with Daiichi Sankyo. The company is backed by investors including Felicis and Y Combinator, and has drawn investment from Freemind and Daewoong Pharmaceutical. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; General Proximity is a drug-discovery company and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time.

providers.name: Grove Biopharma
providers.description: Grove Biopharma is a Chicago-based biopharmaceutical company developing therapeutics that target intracellular protein-protein interactions implicated in cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and rare disorders. The company pioneered Bionic Biologics, hybrid biomolecules that integrate principles of biologic and synthetic design to achieve cell permeability with customizable, modular construction that can disrupt or degrade disease-causing proteins. Grove has demonstrated proof-of-concept against targets including AR/AR-V7, SHOC2, MYC, TAU, and KEAP1/NRF2. Founded in 2025 and led by CEO Geoffrey Duyk, the company raised a $30M Series A in April 2025 and is backed by DCVC. Grove is a therapeutics company with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: VectorY
providers.description: VectorY Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel genetic medicines for neurodegenerative diseases using its proprietary Vectorized Antibody Platform, which combines AAV-based gene delivery with antibody engineering to express therapeutic antibodies directly in the central nervous system. Its pipeline targets amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) with VTx-002 and VTx-001 and Huntington's disease with VTx-003. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a therapeutics research organization, VectorY publishes a corporate website, pipeline, scientific publications, news, and careers, but operates no public developer API, documentation portal, or programmatic interface surface.
